items.body:
Topdown Dialectic’s solo debut bow on False Aralia rounds up over a decade of material in supremely elusive style & pattern - all rug-pulling rhythms and hallucinatory fractals wrapped up with proper, hyperreal frisson. Massive chef’s kiss FFO Vladislav Delay, Beatrice Dillon, Paperclip Minimiser, Purelink, Marc Leclair.

An artist keenly observed since initial gestures on /\\Aught in the early ‘10s, and throughout their cult LP trilogy for Peak Oil during 2018-2021; Topdown Dialectic has become a unique facet of C.21st dub electronics, adored for their grasp of diffused spatio-textural sorcery and wraithlike grooves. Anyone paying close attention to emergent sounds via Peak Oil and its False Aralia offshoot may have guessed at TD’s signature, watermarked imprint on the Borgesian Term EP of late ’25, which can now be confirmed as the work of one and the same Izaak Schlossmann; a photographer and producer patently in possession of heightened proprioceptions and a rewardingly patient approach to lushly dissociative sonification. In other words, he makes some of the sexiest electronic music out there - stuff that genuinely feels like it was made this century - and his latest practically leaves you kissing the sky thru its 80 minutes of lip-biting, skin tingling pressure. 

On 16 tracks timed at exactly 5 minutes each, we’re placed in the presence of suggestive sorcery, eliding unarchived material and jams in a unique ecology of oneiric physics. Never overtly showy or overblown, there’s nevertheless a staggering level of ingenuity and synaesthetic effect to its detailed construction and gaseous fractals resembling the LSD or DMT experience. The label themselves compare its nuance to “the flicker of a candle over a desk of drum machines in a Midwestern basement, or the “first blush of sunlight over a tiny campground as subwoofers creak in the distance”, which proves a perfectly poetic analog to its digitally-smudged refractions and tongue-tip spectral tumescence. 

Ultimately, it’s a singular pleasure to immerse the senses in Topdown Dialectic’s self-contained soundsphere, and never more substantially so than on ‘False LP A’. Longtime enthusiasts will surely recognise his skill in parsing salient aspects of Basic Channel x Rhythm & Sound, and their descendants in Vladislav Delay or Pole, reframing those templates in far more uncertain space with a real animist magick. Each work feels tangibly, ambiguously alive, breathing with dynamics and more voluminous, macro scales, and iridescent with voices and details that commands attentive listeners who will have a field day zoning in/out to its illusive, holographic projections and syncopated chronics.
items._genre: experimental electronic / dub techno / ambient / IDM
items._cn_summary: Topdown Dialectic的首张全长专辑收录了十年间积累的素材，以16首各为5分钟的曲目构建出一个封闭的声音宇宙。制作人Izaak Schlossmann延续其在Peak Oil及分支厂牌False Aralia的一贯路线，将Basic Channel、Rhythm & Sound、Vladislav Delay等dub techno血脉重新置于模糊的时空感中，以缓慢的呼吸感与全息式的声学折射替代传统舞曲结构。专辑不以炫技取胜，而通过气态分形、幽灵般的律动与暧昧的人声细节，模拟一种类似致幻剂体验的通感效应。从极简节奏骨架到宏观动态的层次过渡，每首作品都呈现出独立的张力，既可沉浸式聆听，也适合反复剖析其内部的声音迷宫。独立小厂牌发行，定位明确指向实验电子的深度听众。

items.body:
Late, great Finnish maverick Mika Vainio’s debut ’94 minimal techno masterpiece, originally conceived as Ø, is treated to a much needed reissue, newly expanded with all tracks from the CD on vinyl for the first time and including the absolute all-timer ‘Lasi’ - 100% unmissable if you know what’s good.

Back in circulation 20 years square since the 1st vinyl edition, and just over 30 years since the CD, ‘Metri’ serves a stone cold but heart-melting reminder of Mika’s way with puristic electronics. All 15 tracks from the CD are now cut to vinyl for a definitive edition of Mika’s exemplary solo statement, which would arrive the same year as his debut with Pan Sonic (the ‘Panasonic’ EP). It would dovetail with a time when the original Chicago, NYC and Detroit house and techno templates were being morphed in translation by new waves of artists such as Mika and his pal Ilpo Väisänen, or the likes of Richie Hawtin or Dan Bell, who all effectively streamlined the tekkerz of DJ Pierre, Blake Baxter and Rob Hood to even more stringent levels. 

What distinguishes Mika’s debut as Ø from all of the above is his feel for frosted tone and edge-of-distortion bite, rendered wth resounding plangency; all perhaps stereotypically reflective of his subarctic climes and expressing a sonic personality that would come to define certain strands of electronic music for decades to come, before his untimely passing in 2017, and ever since. We’ve lost count of the times the breathtaking motif of ‘Lasi’ has prompted us to a heads-down, air-punching jack, and reduced rooms at the afters to wide-eyed silent awe, until someone has to ask for an ID. 

Along with the likes of body-bouncing pulse and mind-bending acid tone to ‘Kuvio’ and ‘Twin Bleebs’, the uncanny amniotic ambience of ‘Radio’ and border-watch ambient tension of ‘Kenttä’, or the prototypes for his pure noise works in the ‘JL-CSG’, thru the sublime tension of ‘Dayak’, it’s every bit the ultra classique and we envy anyone coming across this album for the first time. Like many others, we will be taking the opportunity to replace well worn copies with a freshie to rinse and repeat for decades to come.

Seriously this one’s going to the grave with us.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰电子音乐先驱Mika Vainio以Ø名义于1994年发表的首张专辑《Metri》迎来再版，将原CD全部15首曲目首次完整压制黑胶。这张作品以极简电子为骨架，却融入ambient氛围与实验声响设计：冰冷音色与失真边缘的质感、北欧极地式的内省气质贯穿始终。专辑从芝加哥与底特律techno模板出发，提炼出更纯粹的电子语汇，涵盖酸性质感、脉冲律动、子宫般的沉浸氛围以及噪音原型等多重面相。其中《Lasi》以惊人动机成为舞池经典，《Kuvio》《Twin Bleebs》展现身体节奏与迷幻音色的交融，《Kenttä》与《Radio》则散发张力十足的氛围感。该作确立的独特声音个性深刻影响了此后数十年的电子音乐走向，再版提供了一次重新审视这位2017年早逝艺术家遗产的绝佳契机。

items.body:
Remastered reissue of This Heat’s hugely innovative and pioneering anti-rock classic, 1979,  this time on their own, eponymous label. A true milestone in the mutation of pop, rock, avant-garde and electronic music, and arguably post-punk's ground-zero, This Heat consolidated a wealth of music before its arrival whilst casting irrevocable influence over a generation of musicians, producers and engineers in its wake.

Formed in mid ‘70s Brixton, South London, around the trio of Charles Hayward, Charles Bullen and Gareth Williams (later of Flaming Tunes fame), the group drew on and experimented within a flux of sonic disciplines - concrète, pop, dub, and krautrock - to align their mutual ligaments and oppositional structures in a complex, dissonant mass of finely edited improvisations.

Spooling tape noise Testcards jar abruptly with bursts of taut, buzzing drums and metallic guitar squall in Horizontal Hold, before Williams appears as a lamenting ghost, wallowing in the funereal folk drone of Not Waving, and like Damo Suzuki’s shy opposite against the motorik flight of Twilight Furniture.

The album’s definitive moment is still to come, however, with the 2-bar lick of Hayward’s propulsive drums spun thru devilish reverbs and delays in the legendary 24 Track Loop marking a pivotal moment in flux between dub, punk and electro-acoustic music, before the record closes out with Fall of Saigon’s melancholy dirge pop, which clearly set a template for everyone from Hot Chip to Animal Collective or Micachu and the Shapes.

Perhaps understandably, This Heat were never intended as a commercial proposition but, thru the support of John Peel they were able to reach and beguile a national radio audience who probably weren’t ready for them. Thus, their boundary-oblivious virus was planted in the fertile minds of ’79, when punk had already eaten itself and new ideas were definitely required.

By using a minimalist, rhythmically-focussed palette, rent by great minds using the studio-as-instrument, This Heat represents a crucial transition or phase-shift in music from stratified styles toward a union of what might have been formerly perceived as mutually exclusive sounds or styles; boldly following a path out of genre restriction and dilating the dimensions of sonic possibility in the process.

A stone cold classic.
items._genre: post-punk / experimental / avant-garde / dub / krautrock / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这是This Heat 1979年首张同名专辑的再版发行，由乐队自主厂牌发行。乐队由Charles Hayward、Charles Bullen与Gareth Williams三位成员在伦敦Brixton组建，将磁带噪音、具体音乐、dub、krautrock与即兴创作融合为复杂的、不协和的精细剪接声响集合。专辑中磁带测试信号的突跳与紧绷鼓点、嗡鸣吉他并置，随后转入葬礼般的民谣嗡鸣，以Hayward两小节的循环鼓机段落将dub、朋克与电声音乐推向转折点，结尾的悲怆流行曲为后世诸多乐队铺设了模板。评论指出该作将录音室作为乐器使用，跨越类型壁垒，将曾被视为互斥的风格推向融合，是后朋克的源头之一，也是流行、摇滚、先锋与电子音乐交汇的里程碑。

items.body:
Mika Vainio’s swansong Ø album is arguably his solo magnum opus: a deeply personalised set of sonic postcards limning a distant archipelago of discrete sonic isles, ultimately leading to one of his most precious pieces in curtain closer ‘Loputon’ - an ideal epitaph to a peerless and hugely inspirational oeuvre that's become a byword for richly expressive minimalism.

Eight years since the passing of Mika Vainio (1963-2017), the Finnish artist’s formidable yet beautiful spirit lives on in his music with final album ‘Sysivalo’, which was nearing completion before he left this mortal coil far too early. Named as a portmanteau of “sysi” (dark or sinister) and “valo” (light) it locates Vainio inhabiting space between dimensions with an all too profound grasp of metaphysical, musical dark matter, counterweighted with glimpses of the sublime. It sounds closest to our ears in scope and feel to his 2005 masterpiece ‘Kantamoinen’ - a sort of nostalgic reverie for his grandmother - and shares flashes of that LP’s tangibly melancholic pathos tempering and illuminating a sequence of typically ascetic, elemental soundscapes and psychoacoustic sorcery. 

In the short time we’ve spent in its wilds, it’s clear that the post mortem completion, by Rikke Lundgreen and Tommi Grönlund in accordance with Mika’s notes, makes for many welcome returns to its expanse of endless drones and aurora borealis light shows, riddled with pangs of disarmingly gorgeous melody and atmospheric levity. Mika’s knack for giving noise character is in none more gripping effect on the journey thru its 20 vignette-sized chapters, adding up to a mazy mosaic or map of channels and islets for armchair and headphone navigation, weaving from emotionally pregnant panoramic tundras to fragile music box melodies, pitch-bent guitar shimmers and the odd precision-deployed bass pulse.

A northerly breeze puts wind behind noumenal sails on the initial blast of ‘Etudes’, spanning bits of uncannily throaty resonances and harmonic blushes to thawed goth string motifs  and mouth-watering, cavernous bass tones of ‘Etude 5’ and ’Sylvannus.’ At its core ‘Katko’ yields ephemeral fragrances of his gran’s garden, as heard on ‘Kantamoinen’, and felt in the creaking keys of ‘Uusikuu’ or music box wist of ‘Anthem’, whereas the gravelly swill of ’T-Bahn’ is the set’s only beat-driven piece, perhaps his ode to longtime home Berlin, as hinted in the title. And ultimately the final trio of his barely-there title piece, the shine-eyed star-gazer ‘Ursa’ and ‘Loputon (Endless)’ quietly radiate hope in the negative nether; an apt metaphor for all Mika’s work. 'Etudes 4' even uncannily sounds like The Cure's 'If Only Tonight We Could Sleep?' stripped to its barest bones - the closest Mika probably ever came to some ice cold variant of shoegaze.
items._cn_summary: Mika Vainio的遗作《Sysivalo》以芬兰语"sysi"（黑暗）与"valo"（光）的组合命名，定位在两个维度之间的冥想空间。整张专辑由20个短小乐章构成，延续了他2005年作品《Kantamoinen》中对祖母花园的追忆气质，融合持续音、极地光影、脆弱音乐盒旋律与失谐吉他闪烁。录音中以嗓音共振、哥特弦乐、洞穴感低音为主的《Etudes》组曲占据开篇，中段《Katko》《Uusikuu》《Anthem》散发着对故土的怀旧气息，唯一的节奏驱动曲目《T-Bahn》暗指他长期居住的柏林。终曲三段以微弱光芒与无尽回响作结，映射其毕生创作中"黑暗中的希望"核心命题。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi's kraut-techno-free jazz magnum opus is back for its 10th anniversary -  an ambitious ensemble piece featuring an all-star list of players including Ricardo Villalobos, Keith Fullerton Whitman, Mark Fell, crys Cole, Will Guthrie, Arto Lindsay and Konrad Sprenger... Wooooo

You've got to admire Ambarchi's chutzpah here. 'Hubris' is an all you can eat buffet of his various musical cravings, a chance for his friends, influences and collaborators to flex a little and for Ambarchi to attempt to ride the groove like an experienced cowboy on an out-of-control bucking bronco. The first side is the biggest surprise, a dedication to Wang Chung's enduring, disco-influenced 'To Live and Die in L.A.' soundtrack that begins with ping-ponging guitar notes and Jim O'Rourke's synth blips, before elusive Berlin-based composer Konrad Sprenger (aka Joerg Hiller) drops in with some motorized guitar vamps. It's rhythmic gear that fits in with the Berlin school until Mark Fell appears in the final third with some typically fractured percussion.

On the flip, the groove loosens after a short guitar interlude. Ricardo Villalobos takes over with a suitably winding, minimal throb over live rhythms played by Joe Talia and Will Guthrie simultaneously as krautrock techno mutates into disco fusion. Keith Fullerton Whitman tries to nudge the track off the rails with his modular expositions, but the path is set - Arto Lindsay's axe is just the icing on the cake. By the end of the side, we're in full jazz-noise mode: everything's still pegged to Villalobos' central pulse, but that's the only element that's bolted down. 

Hard to believe it's 10 years already - we can't think of a better skeleton key to unlock the secrets behind Black Truffle's musical identity.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Oren Ambarchi的十年纪念再版，汇集了Ricardo Villalobos、Keith Fullerton Whitman、Mark Fell、Arto Lindsay等多位音乐家共同演绎的宏大合奏作品。A面以王冲乐队《To Live and Die in L.A.》配乐为灵感起点，弹跳式吉他音符与Jim O'Rourke的合成器声响交织，随后Konrad Sprenger引入机械化吉他段落，Mark Fell以破碎化打击乐收尾。B面Villalobos接管主导，以极简脉冲节奏与Joe Talia、Will Guthrie的现场打击形成对话，Whitman试图以模块化音色将作品推离轨道，Arto Lindsay的吉他则锦上添花。整体从柏林学派节奏逐步滑入自由爵士与噪音交织的领域，仅Villalobos的脉冲作为稳定锚点。评论指出，这张作品是理解Black Truffle厂牌音乐身份的关键。

items.body:
Holy moly, this is fire! Released by Heat Crimes in collaboration with Thessaloniki's Elhellell label, ‘Paradise Metal’ introduces the fretless electric guitar devotionals of Father Dionysios Tabakis, a 52 year old priest from the historic Greek city of Nafplio, who voices Byzantine church songs in a mix of amp worship hymns and outernational trance movements akin to Sir Richard Bishop or Sandy Bull via László Hortobágyi at Christian Love Forum’s sunday skool. WTF gear of the highest calibre…

‘Paradise Metal’ is one of many reasons why we keep reiterating: Heat Crimes is one of the best labels out there right now. At more than one point did we have to pinch ourselves at the the holy father’s procession of epiphanies effortlessly bridging ancient, microtonal Byzantine modes with DIY electronic modernism, often in jaw-dropping juxtapositions; sublime new age ambient to shoe-gazy basslines and mountaintop guitar shreds to techno incantations. Honestly it’s floored us in so many ways and is bound to exert the same effect with any of you lot, especially if you’re on a mission to sniff out incredible music from unknown margins.

The dozen songs speak richly to Father Dionysios Tabakis’ life immersed in the Orthodox church, and namely the historic Church of Panagitsa in Nafplio (Nativity of the Theotokos), one of the oldest and most beautiful in a city renowned as a centre of Greek faith. There, he has devoted a life to studying music and writing books, applying Athonite monastic wisdom to contemporary concerns of alienation, depression, and isolation in his writings -  which also feed directly into his extraordinary music. 

On a dozen songs the Holy Father proves as fluidly adept at a range of traditional Byzantine instruments (qanun, oud, cümbüş, Politikon tanbur, yali tanbur, ney, zurna, clarinet, Politiki lyra, Pontic lyra, kabak kemane) as his signature fretless guitar, favoured for its ability to feel out microtones - semi or quarter-tone pitches - closest to the human voice. The result is a level of emotional expression and harmonic colour that often escapes western modes, transcending a range of Asia Minor and Mediterranean styles from maqam to Greek traditional and Byzantine music with a disciplined but rapturous sense of transcendence.

Suffice it to say it all adds up to one of the most singular recordings we’ve heard in recent memory, knocking our heads clean off with flashbacks to the likes of Sandy Bull’s modal psych-folk, or even Sunn O))) x Julian Cope and Sun City Girls/Sir Richard Bishop ritualism in the first half, and traversing in the 2nd to astonishing sorts of techno impressionism, as with the THX string shear and choral chant of ‘TECHNO σε ΜΟΝΑΣΤΗΡΙ’ and a whole new definition of trance-techno, thru to bits that sound like a Greek Enya. 

100% brilliant, out there music.
items._genre: experimental / Byzantine chant / fretless guitar / electronic ritual / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 52岁希腊东正教神父Father Dionysios Tabakis首张专辑，将拜占庭教会圣咏与无品电吉他即兴、DIY电子实验及地中海传统器乐（乌德、卡侬、奈伊、克拉里内、潘都里拉琴等）编织在一起。无品电吉他擅长捕捉四分之一音等微分音程，与人声及古调式形成紧密共振。十二首曲目横跨新纪元氛围、鞋失真低音线、山巅吉他狂飙与techno咒语般的第二段落，风格从桑迪·布尔的调式迷幻民谣滑向Sunn O)))式的仪式感，最终抵达techno印象派与希腊版Enya式的恍惚电子领域。由Heat Crimes与塞萨洛尼基Elhellell联合发行，标签为小型独立厂牌。录音将阿索斯山修道院的灵性智慧转化为对当代疏离、抑郁与孤绝议题的回应，是边缘地带罕见的精神音乐实践。

items.body:
In physical stature and imaginative scope, Luc Ferrari’s 10 x CD / 11 Hour selection for INA GRM’s series presents a poetic building block of C.20th electronic music from the founding director of the GRM in 1958, presenting a unique art history spanning six decades of ingenious, beguiling soundcraft.

Part of a legendary series including titles by concrète pioneers Pierre Schaefer & Pierre Henry, plus weighty surveys of Bernrad Parmegiani, Éliane Radigue and François Bayle, this lavish boxset of Luc Ferrari’s work is a masterclass exploration of avant garde form and function that charts experimental music’s research and development during a radical phase. While even the notion of such a large storage device for sound was unimaginable when Ferrari began making his cut-up musical collages and sound poetry in the ‘50s, his ‘L’Œuvre Électronique’ covers the progression of musical technology and thought from its most laboriously executed origins, working with tape and raw blocks of sound, to the grander digital staging of his ‘90s and early ‘00s radio plays, plotted for multiple voices and spatialised landscapes. 

Collected, this set forms an incredible deep dive into art-music history where the materiality of sound is questioned and reconsidered in relief of its musical connotations, creating in the process a peerless body of work that better approximates the texture of dreams or the audness of waking life than any song, and has long informed the approach to sound organisation by a host of progressive artists, effectively bridging the conceptual precedents of Varèse and Cage and the contemporary futures projected by Lee Gamble or Valerio Tricoli.

The 98 tracks from 31 releases, clocking up just over 10 hours of recordings, delineate across decades following Ferrari’s studies with Messaien and Honegger in the mid ‘50s, and a period of illness that made him better acquainted with the radio receiver, and pioneers such as Schöneberg and Webern, to his co-founding of the Groupe de Recherches Musicales with Schaeffer and François-Bernard Mâche in 1958, and thru his landmark transformation of field recordings made on a Yugoslavian beach, and the ravishing abstractions of later electronic works. 

Until his passing, aged 76 in Arezzo, Italy, Ferrari remained ceaselessly active both in his own practice and teaching, and was revered as the poet of musique concrète. He bought a particularly gallic purview to the paradigm, especially when considered against the more hard-nosed academic pursuits of his peers, making singular use of vocals as an elusive or sometimes literal presence in his works in a way that others didn’t, and as such his works all hare a certain liminal quality that appears richly seductive to fans of fantasy storytelling as much as psychedelic soundtracks and sound as dreamfood imagery.

items._cn_summary: 这套十碟装合辑收录了Luc Ferrari横跨五十余年的电子音乐创作，作为INA GRM系列的里程碑之作，呈现了他从五十年代磁带拼贴与声音诗学起步，逐步走向九十年代数字广播剧与空间化声景的完整轨迹。合辑涵盖九十八首作品，梳理了他在GRM创始人Pierre Schaeffer门下受训的经历，以及他在南斯拉夫海滩进行的标志性田野录音实验。Ferrari将声音的物质性从其音乐语义中剥离，构建出贴近梦境质感或清醒生活听觉层次的声响结构，桥接了Varèse与Cage的概念先驱与当代实验艺术家的声音逻辑。其作品的法国式诗性气质、对人声的独特运用，以及在声音拼贴与具象音乐间的自由穿梭，使其在学院派电子音乐传统中独树一帜。

items.body:
The Necks tantalisingly ruminate on stillness, decay and space in an absorbing, opiated follow-up to the windswept momentum of ’Travel’, chasing a quieter dragon into midnight airs shared by Loren Connors, Morton Feldman, that 'Autechre remix of Tortoise's 'To Day Retrieval', Talk Talk, Alice Coltrane.

Australia’s widely revered minimalist jazz / avant garde / electro-acoustic ambient (delete as applicable) troupe lure us right into the depths of their shared psyche with an unmissable invitation to swan the vast inner landscapes of ‘Bleed’. For an unbroken 42 minutes Chris Abrahams’ soft keys elide the shimmering plangency and distant, dreamlike drum rolls of Tony Buck and Lloyd Swanton’s painterly strokes of guitar at a seductive resting heart pace. Gently exploring notions of stasis, entropy, and space, and guided by an incandescent spirit that flickers between melancholy and the sublime, they trustingly navigate that schism with a subtlety that has propelled them since 1989’s classic ‘Sex’, and has left the template wide open for practically all Aussie experimental artists in their lustrous wake. 

Intimate yet expansive, ‘Bleed’ operates on a tongue tip of feeling in an almost palindromic arrangement that rewards repeat plays to supine minds. Chris Abrahams' grasp of extended melodic thought unfolds across the keyboard from right hand starlight to exquisitely sparing notes left to ring out on air like a syrupped Morton Feldman, gradually accreting the cross-hatching of Lloyd Swanton’s post-rock guitar hazes and bells carried on the warm air from Tony Buck, a usually ceentral figure who judiciously takes the back seat here.

Prone to leave languorous lacunæ for the imagination fills in the gaps, the piece proceeds into the most hauntingly sonorous mid section of layered, lingering overtones that hang over the atmosphere like noctilucent clouds, even precipitating a passage of atonal doom. However, they resolve via the padded palpitation of percussion at curiously bittersweet junctures in a coda that effectively leaves the keys to breeze and loop back to the start for anyone ready to go at it again. It’s typically gorgeous stuff, framing the trio at their lower case best.
items._genre: minimalist jazz / avant-garde / electro-acoustic ambient / improvisation
items._cn_summary: The Necks在《Bleed》中以一整段四十二分钟不间断的冥想式即兴，取代前作《Travel》那种疾风式的推进。键盘手轻柔的和弦与吉他稀疏的泛音交织，鼓手退居幕后，仅以远景般的敲击点缀，三人共同营造出一种近乎药物浸泡的悬停感。整首作品以近乎回文的对称结构展开——前段以稀疏的高音音符如星光般铺陈，缓慢汇聚成层叠的中段，笼罩着不协和的暗流与回响，最后在打击乐的低语中回归起始的宁静。评论将其置于Loren Connors、Morton Feldman、Talk Talk与Alice Coltrane的脉络中，强调其以极简与空间感探索停滞与熵的哲学命题。乐队自1989年以来持续深耕此种三人即兴美学，对澳洲实验音乐场景影响深远。

items.body:
Epic 16 hour François Bayle retrospective, an unparalleled document of the key C.20th electro-acoustic and concrète pioneer and director of the hugely influential GRM institution from 1966-1997, where he was instrumental in bringing the Acousmonium speaker array and INA-GRM label to life, among many important, enduring innovations

This 10 year reissue of ’50 Ans d’Acousmagique’ joins INA-GRM’s quintessential boxsets of Pierre Schaeffer, Pierre Henry, Parmegiani, Radigue, and Xenakis in a rare, stellar microcosm of works by twentieth century groundbreakers. At 16 hrs long, and including 228 tracks, it offers a comprehensive overview of François Bayle’s unfathomable catalogue of work between 1972-2012. During this time Bayle was pivotal in altering perceptions of music’s materiality and purpose at the most fundamental and philosophic levels through his work in developing the Acousmonium diffusion system - an “orchestra of loudspeakers” which has become key to the GRM’s facilities in Paris - as well as supporting technological developments (Syter, GRM Tools, Midi Formers, Acousmographe) which are vital to his own remarkable compositions, and his endeavours organising radio broadcasts and events. 

Deeply informing and paralleling the history of recorded electronic music during its formative golden years, Bayle’s recordings render an embarrassment of riches for the discerning and explorative listener and historians of vanguard C.20th music. Between the flighty electro-acoustic staging of his avian dreams on ’72’s ‘Trois Rêves D'oiseau’ to the sensually lathered cosmic delirium of 1978-80’s ‘Erosphère’ works, to his beguiling latter tributes to his tutors at the Paris Conservatoire and Darmstadt summer courses, Messiaen and Stockhausen; the overwhelming scope of Bayle’s work, and thus the boxset, is brought into clearer focus by its chronological sequencing, offering a logical pathway thru his incredible projections of imagination.

It bears reflection that figures such as François Bayle created, and then opened, doors of perception for music in the past century that have come to mirror and shape the soundsphere we now inhabit. His innovations in sound spatialisation and the embrace of an acoustic unknown, or acousmagique, underline some of the most fascinating expressions of pathos thru art in our lifetimes, and this boxset is more than enough to send heads reeling into deep time for eons to come.
items._genre: acousmatic / musique concrète / electro-acoustic / electronic / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这套16小时、228曲的盒装合辑系统梳理了法国电子声学先驱弗朗索瓦·拜尔自1972至2012年间近半个世纪的创作轨迹。拜尔作为GRM掌门人（1966-1997），不仅主持开发了改变声音空间化思维的Acousmonium扬声器阵列，还推动了Syter、GRM Tools、Acousmographe等关键技术的诞生。盒装按时间顺序排列，收录从1972年鸟类梦境般的早期电声作品《Trois Rêves D'oiseau》，到70年代末《Erosphère》中带有宇宙迷醉感的声音探索，再到向梅西安与施托克豪森致敬的后期作品，涵盖其声音物质性与哲学性的核心命题。与INA-GRM此前推出的谢菲尔、亨利、帕尔梅贾尼、拉迪格、泽纳基斯等大师盒装形成互文，是20世纪先锋音乐史不可替代的档案文献。

items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国-肯尼亚打击乐手Sven Kacirek与83岁肯尼亚传统dodo歌唱家Ogoya Nengo的合作。音乐以Kacirek的Buchla合成器、手鼓和架子鼓为骨架，托起Nengo与Olith Ratengo相互抛接的人声。合成器多层次切分节奏在听感上几乎隐形，到歌曲结束时已与声部浑然一体。技术始终服务于人声，从不喧宾夺主，但会在声线最紧绷处突然涌出棱角分明的失真。专辑体现了传统与现代的真正对话：83岁歌手首次走向全球舞台，与电子节奏中的白人乐手同台，让根源音乐获得前卫质地，使创新听起来仿佛已有千年历史。

items.excerpt: Structura Parva — literally “small structure” — acts as both title and manifesto. Seven years after Forma, the Italian duo Filtro (Luca de Biasi and Angelo Bignamini) have moved away from long-form improvisations built from concrete sounds and electrical interference towards something more concentrated, deliberate, and architectural. Across six concise pieces, they construct miniature sonic ecosystems from the sparsest of materials, embracing self-imposed limitations as catalysts for invention.
items.body: Structura Parva — literally “small structure” — acts as both title and manifesto. Seven years after Forma, the Italian duo Filtro (Luca de Biasi and Angelo Bignamini) have moved away from long-form improvisations built from concrete sounds and electrical interference towards something more concentrated, deliberate, and architectural. Across six concise pieces, they construct miniature sonic ecosystems from the sparsest of materials, embracing self-imposed limitations as catalysts for invention. Working with only a handful of sounds per track, Filtro adopt an approach reminiscent of Oulipo’s creative constraints, treating composition as a process of exploring the possibilities contained within a tightly defined framework. Yet the result never feels academic. The sounds themselves remain stubbornly alive: intermittent clicks, fragile drones, processed acoustic fragments and high-frequency traces evolve, misbehave and interact in ways that resist predictable looping or repetition. Rather than expanding ideas through scale, Filtro trace how small gestures ripple through space, giving the EP a sense of depth and movement. What distinguishes Structura Parva is its refusal of sonic flattening. Every sound retains its material presence and tactile character, whether emerging from a sampler, field recordings or processed everyday objects. The duo’s attention to dynamics and spatial placement ensures that even the sparsest passages feel animated by hidden tensions. These are not static minimal compositions but living structures, constantly shifting beneath the surface. The EP’s subtitle of sorts — “sounds for night reflections and dark disquiets” — feels apt. There is a subdued melancholy running throughout the record, but also curiosity and attentiveness. By reducing their palette and abandoning improvisation in favour of meticulous composition, Filtro have created their most focused work to date: a quietly compelling study in how much emotional weight can be carried by the smallest of structures. In the following interview Angelo Bignami and Luca de Biasi explain their working process. Structura Parva feels like a significant shift from the long-form improvisation for concrete sounds and electrical interferences of Forma towards much shorter and more concentrated pieces. What led you to embrace these “small structures”? Was this reduction a deliberate aesthetic decision or the natural outcome of your evolving practice? Luca de Biasi: After Forma, we took a long break to dedicate ourselves to our solo work, which also gave us the opportunity to reflect on what we wanted Filtro to become. The idea was to work meticulously on individual sounds, processing them and finding affinities with other sounds to shape the pieces. We set a strict limit: just two sounds each and nothing else. The biggest change for me was using a sampler, which allowed me to process sound differently than in the past and focus on individual sounds before looking at the whole picture. We also worked extensively on dynamics and the movement of sound in space. In some tracks, this remained direct, while in others we added the natural echoes of the different environments where we re-recorded the pieces. Angelo Bignamini: It was a bit of both. It represents an evolution of our sound, moving away from what were initially uncontrolled, improvisation-based impulses toward actual composition focused on a few core elements. I believe this shift was influenced by our shared listening habits at the time, as well as a mutual desire to produce something more focused and structured. The EP is described as reflecting a new approach to “minimal structures and small electronics.” What does “small electronics” mean for Filtro in practical and conceptual terms? Are you interested in intimacy, scale, fragility, or perhaps a different relationship between sound and space? L: The new approach was all about working on individual sounds before the whole composition. In practice, I used a modular synthesizer consisting simply of an oscillator, a complex envelope, and a filter, constantly tweaking the sound until I achieved a satisfactory result. I did the same using very simple field recordings. As I mentioned, the choice of individual sounds, their interaction, and their interconnectivity were the core ideas behind the project. A: It is called “small electronics” simply because the entire project is built on just a few elements—each track develops across two or three layers at most—and an extremely minimal setup. Often, we are just using everyday objects or small acoustic instruments, which we record and process using a sampler and a laptop. The core idea was to maximize the value of each individual sound and distribute it throughout the space, which inevitably transforms both its signifier and its signified. Both of you have long been interested in sound detached from its original context and meaning. On Structura Parva, the sounds often seem stripped down to traces, gestures and subtle interactions. How do you decide when a sound has been reduced enough, and how do you prevent minimalism from becoming merely an exercise in subtraction? L: For this latest project, each individual sound was developed separately by Angelo and me. We both worked on our own ideas without any prior agreement. After months of work, we decided it was time to meet up and listen to what we had done. Choosing which sounds to use was ultimately quite simple and quick. I don’t know how, but the work each of us had done seemed to share a common goal. A: Honestly, I didn’t really worry about that problem. The goal was simply to find minimal structures that could convey emotional meaning—which, in a way, is a prerequisite for any kind of music. There is almost always a rhythmic element, a background texture or drone, and a melodic element. If you look past the totally hallucinated style, we aren’t actually that far off from a traditional song structure. Angelo’s work frequently explores deterioration, tape processes and feedback, while Luca’s practice involves modular synthesis and improvisation. How has the dialogue between these approaches changed since Forma? Has the balance between improvisation and composition shifted over the years? L: Our approach has always been improvisational. We used to meet for long sessions and then extract the sections that would become the final work. This time, it was different: we worked on the tracks individually, then discussed them and decided together which parts made sense when combined. We then re-recorded them in various environments to give them depth. We also placed great importance on the movement of sounds in space. Therefore, this latest work is much more compositional than our previous ones. A: In this latest work, there is absolutely nothing improvised. We worked in perfect sync on the individual tracks, with each of us utilizing our own sounds and processing techniques. What united us was a shared vision to produce something simple and circular, yet containing an internal evolution driven primarily by how the individual layers intersect. Nothing was left to chance, except for the deliberate use of random modulations and stereophonic automation. The EP is presented as “sounds for night reflections and dark disquiets.” There is a strong sense of restraint and suspended tension throughout the six tracks. Were there particular emotional states, environments or listening situations that informed the album, or do you prefer to leave such associations entirely in the hands of the listener? L: There were certainly external factors that influenced the choice and development of the sound—not necessarily musical ones. In my case, books had a significant impact, changing my approach to life and, consequently, to music. Using a sampler also definitely allowed me to focus more on single sounds. However, I prefer not to give listeners any specific direction regarding our influences, so that their listening experience remains entirely unique and personal. A: The way people interpret tracks is one of the most incredible wonders of music. Because of that, I prefer to let listeners filter the pieces however they choose and place them in whatever context feels right to them. Personally, I feel these sounds express themselves best in a nighttime setting, but that is by no means a strict rule. (Gianmarco Del Re)
items._cn_summary: 意大利二人组 Filtro 在前作《Forma》七年之后推出《Structura Parva》，从长篇具体声音即兴转向高度凝练的微型结构。整张 EP 仅由六首短曲组成，每首曲目严格限制在两种声音素材之内，融合采样器处理、田野录音与日常物件声响。评论指出声音始终保有物质质感与触觉特征，间歇性咔嗒声、脆弱的低频嗡鸣、高频痕迹在空间中相互作用，动态层次与空间定位赋予稀疏段落以隐藏张力。整体笼罩在沉静忧郁与夜间冥想氛围中，通过严谨的作曲手法探索最少材料所能承载的最大情感重量，被视为该组合迄今最具聚焦力的作品。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — After debuting in 2021 with one of Brazil's strangest contributions to the world of zeuhl metal, theJo�o Pessoa based PAPANGU jettisoned the metallic edge of its debut "Holocene" with its follow up"Lampi�o Rei" which followed in 2024 with more of a classic progressive rock approach mixed with thesounds of Brazil ranging from forro, xaxado and udigrudi. The band returns with its Brazilianbravado cocktail of prog and local flavors with its third installment CELESTIAL which features a 10-track concept that once again steers its sound into a new direction. Trimming down from a sextet toa five-member outfit, CELESTIAL follows suit with the metal aspects deemphasized (although stillpresent) and more retro warmth evoked through the use of analog equipment and a passion for bringingthe likes of jazz fusion, symphonic prog, zeuhl and other classic prog influences to this Brazilianstreet party.Another main feature of this third musical expedition is that on CELESTIAL the vocals are ratherdownplayed with crafty instrumental complexities nurturing warm inviting melodies into displays ofprog majesty evoking the elegance of 70s jazz fusion, the artifice of Gentle Giant complexities andthe sneaky labyrinthine excursionist proclivities that nurtured intuited perspicacity throughmusical obstacle courses that never lose their soul and of course all fortified with the true joiede vie that only Brazilian musical styles can deliver. It's a triumphant return to a new form afterwhat sounded to me like a clunky and disjointed sophomore offering. More focused and refined,CELESTIAL may not deliver the supposed concept of a bandit on a mission to prevent an ecologicaldisaster in some undisclosed form but for what the story narrative lacks in heft, the musicalprowess more than compensates for.CELESTIAL may share an album title with the post-metal band Isis but delivers a truer musical vibeof heavenly bliss with the Rhodes piano and vintage keyboard sounds leading the way. Add someunexpected sound effects from a rubber chicken and Brazilian folk instruments and it's easy to getsucked into the majesty of CELESTIAL's intricate flow of modern modern meets retro with a sensiblerunning time of just over 50 minutes. The album's energy bursts into full gear on the opening "Mau-Olhado" and continues its journey of jubilee throughout the album's ten distinct installments. Awaft of classic Canterbury is present throughout evoking the warmth of that classic Egg / SoftMachine / Hatfield & The North along with occasional bursts of heavier rock that emulates blackmetal (at least in the vocal department) all creatively wrapped in the retro prog padding that keepsthe album amazingly well balanced.Tracks like "Fechamento de Corpo" exhibit the band's menagerie of modernity with staccato basedgrooves fortified with crazy contrapuntal effects and a zeuhl-esque propulsion system that allowsthe cadences and motifs to cozy up together snuggly like a den of hibernating mammals. While theprevious works had me wondering if PAPANGU was primarily a one hit wonder with its out of the gatecrashing the prog party debut, CELESTIAL puts those concerns to rest with a beautifully deliveredprocession of tones and timbres executed in crafty compositions that find the band a form ofmaturation that seemed to be lost on "Lampi�o Rei." Throughout this smorgasbord of retro prog onecan detect moments of classic Yes, Genesis, Gentle Giant, Weather Report, Egg and the list goes onhowever PAPANGU also ekes out modernities with excellent production value and 21st century jazzplaybook tricks. While the metal felt out of balance on the previous album, here the subordinateeffects are instigated perfectly without the bombast ruining the dynamic flow. A brilliant thirdalbum here!
items._genre: experimental progressive / zeuhl / Brazilian fusion / jazz-rock
items._cn_summary: 巴西乐队PAPANGU的第三张专辑延续其对前卫摇滚的探索，放弃了首张作品的金属锋芒，转向以模拟设备营造复古温度的路线。专辑将爵士融合、坎特伯雷派、辛弗尼克（zeuhl）律动与巴西本土音乐元素（forró、xaxado、民间乐器）熔于一炉，并加入橡胶鸡等意外音效制造荒诞感。编曲上大量运用复调对位与爵士和声，键盘与 Rhodes 电钢琴主导音色，人声被刻意弱化以突出器乐复杂性。叙事围绕一位匪徒试图阻止生态灾难的概念展开，虽然故事性略显单薄，但音乐本身的精密度弥补了这一不足。十首作品贯穿始终，保持约五十分钟的紧凑结构，是一支兼具地方色彩与前卫胆识的乐队在融合方向上更为成熟的呈现。

items.body: Becoming a new person Leaving just a trace behind What Nationalists want to avoid That is what I do now Roman Wilhelm began making music in 1991 with the sort of recording setup that encourages either ingenuity or surrender: two ghetto blasters, a teenage bedroom, and no obvious reason to believe anyone beyond its walls would ever hear the results. Born in 1976 in a small West German town, Wilhelm had recorded his first song by the time he was fifteen. A demo tape eventually found its way to a local goth DJ, who invited him to perform at a small dark-music festival. There remained the practical matter of instrumentation. Wilhelm did not own a synthesizer, so he brought his Italian accordion. That solution says quite a bit about the sensibility behind roman946, Wilhelm’s long-running musical project, where the machinery of post-punk and electronic music has always been susceptible to interruption by something tactile, eccentric, or stubbornly homemade. The accordion was hardly an adolescent anomaly. During his years studying graphic design in Halle (Saale), Wilhelm began collaborating with aspiring filmmakers, composing music for images before gradually moving toward a broader conception of performance. After relocating to Berlin in 2005, he found himself drawn into the city’s art world, playing gallery openings and treating music, at times, as an exhibit with its own spatial and conceptual logic. His new album, Balta, gathers those seemingly separate histories into one body of work. Songwriting sits beside electronics; programmed structures are interrupted by acoustic instruments; post-punk economy brushes against folk music and experimental composition. Wilhelm cites Onuka, Laurie Anderson, Lou Reed, The Legendary Pink Dots, and And Also The Trees among his inspirations, a list broad enough to suggest that taxonomy has never been his preferred occupation. The album’s geography is equally expansive. Balta looks toward Germany and Eastern Europe at a moment when political anxiety has become increasingly difficult to leave outside the rehearsal room. Wilhelm addresses the rise of the political right in Germany, intolerance, artistic freedom, gender stereotypes, and the unease surrounding developments farther east, drawing much of the material from events he has witnessed and conversations with people whose lives intersect with these pressures. His working life gives those concerns an unusual proximity. Wilhelm divides his professional time between the German Institute of Economic Research and the Berlin University of the Arts, moving between debates over social policy and questions about artistic independence. Those worlds find their way into songs such as BBC and into the wonderfully peculiar phrase Lead me to Ambivalentopia, which may be as good a name as any for the continent Wilhelm is attempting to describe. Wilhelm speaks eloquently about his songs: The Beach (Daina #1) “The album begins with a Daina, a traditional Latvian genre of song and poetry consisting of four lines, often employing diminutives (Balta, balta debestiņa (little white sky), gaidu, gaidu vasariņu (waiting for the little summer), koki klusē vērojot (trees watching in silence), melnus kuģus jūriņā (black fleet in the little sea)). After the central motif, which uses cellos and guitars to evoke the motion of waves, addresses geopolitical uncertainties, the loud finale resolves the tension through absurd acts of defiance. The final line abruptly switches from English to French and Chinese.” The plodding beat and horns give this spoken word track a deep gravity, almost bordering on psychedelic. Aufbruch “A Jungle rhythm never fully unfolds in this song; repeatedly stutters to a halt, prompting uncoordinated flailing rather than dancing. The bass holds together elements that the piano, synths, and guitar seem unable to reconcile. Hovering over it all is the vocal, which also fails to strictly adhere to the beat. A German story of flight leads to the question of how the grandchild generation would treat refugees today; it identifies intolerant, right-wing behaviour as a negative dimension of flight. Both vocals and lyrics are indirectly influenced by Hildegard Knef and Nico Pfäffgen, particularly in the way they handle the interplay between banality and the dramatic. The song is based on an authentic poem about fleeing Silesia and the subsequent experience of social exclusion in the Federal Republic of Germany.” BBC “This simply structured post-punk theme, driven by a central guitar riff, centers on a person trapped in academic gender clichés.” Chimes and motorik beats bolster this track, which sounds like a lost Fad Gadget track. I Need Nida “A melancholic motif emerges, shaped by the imprecise playing of an analog synthesizer with faulty filters. We observe the protagonist, Katya, a dissident from Kaliningrad as she builds a new life as an artist in her adopted home of Armenia. The abrupt onset of the chorus underscores the fact that homesickness knows no borders. The song was inspired by a text message from the real-life Katya (I asked her where she was going, all she said is: I need Nida).” Ambivalentopia “Berlin-style electro-post-punk meets the stark juxtaposition of multilingual names for various border towns, some situated at the heart of current political events, others far detached from the global stage. The convergence of multiple languages seems to obscure the message, yet invites the listener to seek it out in the spaces in between: the dream of a world where one is no longer limited to simply choosing one out of several names.” This track has a heavily Kraftwerk-inspired chant and backbeat that will get stuck in your head. Exchange; KWC “Being an academic exchange coordinator for Berlin University of the Arts, I deal with the questions raised in “Exchange” on a daily basis: What is openness? How does tolerance emerge? Is time abroad mostly about partying? Where do you go? Is there an atmosphere of openness? Two verses present a caricatured juxtaposition of utopia and dystopia before the language abruptly switches to Chinese in the final chorus. With its hard, driving drum’n’bass sound, “KWC” contrasts sharply with the lyrics: a belated, self-reproachful letter to a deceased friend.” Hotel “An old clock sets the tempo for the album’s most oppressive track; an accordion and an electric piano seem to be chasing the seconds. It tells the true story of a hotelier in a small Saxon town who aggressively tries to justify to the narrator why he did not turn away a group of fascists arriving for a conference (After all, what was he supposed to do? Hardly anyone visited them anymore, and he was left alone with the fascists in the hotel). That clock is ticking very loudly right now, too, in the run-up to the elections in Saxony-Anhalt, where right-wing populist AfD is campaigning for an abolishment of compulsory education, and for the eviction of all foreigners, whoever they may be.” An Old Fort; Take This Town (Daina #2) “Listeners are taken on a spoken-word tour through the overgrown ruins of Kostrzyn (Küstrin). The concluding fragment, “Daina #2,” tells the story of a refugee from Ukraine currently in Latvia (We ordered drinks, I heard her say: “If I don’t drink, I can’t sleep”. Age seventeen). The musical concept, collapses in on itself at the end. Listen to Balta below and order the album here. items.body: Statiqbloom Splintered Fingers self-released Fade Kainer’s Statiqbloom has two fairly distinct eras; the electro-industrial years spanning from the project’s foundation in 2014 to around 2020, and the more freeform era (the beginning of which coincided roughly with Kainer’s move to Berlin from Brooklyn) which explore industrialized techno, dark ambient, and rhythmic noise, amongst other sounds. New album Splintered Fingers situates itself between the latter styles handily, unifying them via Statiqbloom’s propensity for blackened textures and depressive ambience. Whether or not Kainer set out to split the difference on the album isn’t clear, but there are plenty of callbacks to his recent history, often reconstituted and recontextualized for effect. “Salt the Flower (stripped back version)” takes the noisy and clamorous cut from recent Hands Production release The Casket Nest and carves away the beats, leaving only reverbed drones, half-chanted vocals and ominous waves of feedback that threatens to drag the whole song under. It’s quite reminiscent of the work he was doing on Winter, although the extremity of its sound, shared by cuts like the brief “Threshold” and the thrumming “Sedated Presence” bring to mind his Kain LP for Sonic Groove. Still, Kainer is ever reluctant to sit still for any period of time, and there are hints of new directions sprinkled throughout the proceedings. Opener “Grave Procession” feels like a classic powernoise cut in its rhythm, but the thick layer of saturation that sits atop its relentless tempo has a sort of smothering tension to it, like the beats are slowly being churned into nothing as the song goes on. Alternately, on “Groundless” the slow tempo and funereal pads have the same sensibility as much of the witch house revival sound, albeit with a nod to the lo-fi sound of early black metal. While not new in terms of sonics, they’re certainly formations we haven’t heard Kainer try his hand at explicitly, and could easily prove to be fertile ground for the prolific artist. Like most of Statiqbloom’s 2020’s output, Splintered Fingers is about mood above all else; even on the record’s centerpiece track “H.O.M.K.V. (live)”, an eight minute excursion into some truly gnarly beats and shouted vocals, there’s a bleak strain of pained emotion that informs the proceedings. Regardless of whatever sounds Fade Kainer is trying his hand at, his particular brand of rage and woe will mark it as his own. Splintered Fingers by STATIQBLOOM The post Statiqbloom, “Splintered Fingers” appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items.body:
Colour us enchanted with this otherworldly hour of airborne flute, Saw-U, vocal and drum spirits sourced from the night markets, museum shops and cafés of Laos, by Gary Sullivan ov Bodega Pop, who aptly compares them with Laurent Jeanneau’s forays in the same zone of interest for Akuphone & Sublime Frequencies. Check for the uncanny frissons of ‘Lam Cheung’ and its slew of piquant percussive works, all shimmering with the type of timeless lustre we’ve come to expect from Sullivan & DINTE’s magpie picks...

"In Lao PDR, music was seemingly everywhere. Walking through an open field outside Savannakhet to the sound of someone playing a khaen on a distant porch, the bracing rush of electronic molam from of one of Vientiane’s many aging malls, the awkward blending of the blind so u player’s voice with the bustling sounds of Luang Prabang’s night market.

It was in that UNESCO World Heritage Site that I found most of the CDs and CD-Rs from which I’ve ripped the tracks for this compilation. I’m almost certain I picked up a thumb drive at the night market that held many hours of additional music that could have been included, but if so, I’ve misplaced it, lost it for good, or simply misremember purchasing it in the first place. What I do remember is that these discs were literally the last copies in the cafe, museum, bookstore, and night market where I bought them, and not all of them played all the way through without sonic deterioration.

The sounds compiled here play in stark contrast to the more contemporary recordings I found in Laos, most of which featured some form of upbeat digital workstation molam or children’s songs. In addition to the ever-present khaen, this collection includes recordings of the sanai, a single-reed instrument fashioned from a water buffalo horn, the ceremonial khong nyai gong, the pi and similar free-reeds, and at least a dozen more traditional instruments played by Lao and ethnic minority artists. While some of these tracks were laid down in Vientiane or Luang Prabang, most were recorded near where the artists lived, from the legendary Vat Phou in the far south to the former Pathet Lao capital Xam Neua in the northeast.

Unlike Laurent Jeanneau’s more focused Lao collections for Akuphone and Sublime Frequencies, which remain among my favorite albums of all time, the present cassette-only selection is literally all over the PDR map. The sequencing is entirely in response to rhythm and texture and includes recordings from the 1970s, 80s, 90s, and early aughts. This may frustrate those with more of an ethnomusicology bent, but my hope is that the listener experiences something akin to wandering for the first time through this majestic country, encountering the last copies of forgotten recordings one after another, and hearing in these remains fragments of the past and a living musical landscape."

–Gary Sullivan (Bodega Pop)”
items._genre: world music / traditional folk / field recording / Lao traditional
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Bodega Pop的Gary Sullivan策划，收录了老挝各地夜市、博物馆商店和咖啡馆中流散的传统音乐录音，时间跨度从1970年代至2000年代初。内容涵盖卡亨笛、单簧水牛角萨奈、锣群等多种民族乐器，既有万象和琅勃拉邦的录音，也包括从南部瓦普寺到东北部前巴特寮首都桑怒等地的现场捕捉。编译者以节奏与质感为线索进行编排，刻意打破地域与年代的严格分类，试图让听众获得漫步老挝、偶然翻找遗失唱片的沉浸式听觉体验。收录曲目多为最后存世的稀有拷贝，部分唱片存在播放损耗与音质劣化的问题。Sullivan强调这并非系统性的民族音乐学研究，而是以个人收藏与文化漫游为出发点的感性汇编，与Laurent Jeanneau为Akuphone和Sublime Frequencies所做的更聚焦的老挝采录形成对比。

items.body:
KAKUHAN / Sara Udon cellist Yuki Nakagawa takes a solemn yet dreamlike debut solo bow on the Unheard of Hope label - home to Mabe Fratti -  intently focussed on holistic examinations of his instrument, revealing its inner voices via various raw and processed strategies. RIYL Leila Bordreuil, Ecka Mordecai, Hildur Guðnadóttir, Okkyung Lee or Judith Hamann.

It's hard to explain just how eerily familiar Nakagawa's playing is, but you'll understand what we mean after hearing just a few moments of 'You Haze - I'. We've grown fully accustomed to the way Nakagawa handles the cello without even realizing it, absorbing his technique on records from KAKUHAN, his duo project with Koshihiro Hino, and Sara Udon alongside Naarm duo CS + Kreme. The way Nakagawa rests his bow between tones, picking up animated off-notes that make his sustained drones sound deep, dark and resonant, is genuinely personal, identifiable immediately. And although that aspect of his performance is front and center on his debut's opening track, it's the additional elements that tip us over the edge: the discreet, theremin-like wails that occupy a space just in the corner of the composition. 

After establishing his signature, Nakagawa veers away from his own convention sharply on 'CHU-MA', plucking the cello's strings and bending them as if they were attached to a koto. It's all remarkably stark at first, without much enhancement from Nakagawa's pedals and he slowly teases in different sounds that widen the instrument's range: woody creaks, knocks and growls that fill out its body and piercing overtones that go beyond the usual confines of the strings. Somehow, even using all these extended techniques, Nakagawa still manages to make music that's effortlessly enjoyable. It's bumpy, self-consciously experimental material, but not without roots - maybe best compared to Fred Frith's 'Guitar Solos' or Hans Reichel's 'The Death of the Rare Bird'.

There's even a prettiness to tracks like 'Upper and under the bridge' and 'You Haze - II' that betrays Nakagawa's resolve. But he's best when he's operating on the far fringe, turning his cello into a drum kit on the rickety, brilliant 'Grey test hits' or a vast resonator on the perplexingly huge 'Sange / Tsuki', an 8-minute xenharmonic spiral that sounds like an orchestra of fingerdrummed steel pans and a set of metal sheets being bowed in a concrete cavern. There's nothing else quite like it, we're sure of that.

items._cn_summary: 中川由纪（大提琴手）在这张首张个人专辑中深入探索大提琴的内在声音，通过原始演奏与电子处理相结合的策略，呈现了一系列富有冥想气质又实验性强烈的作品。评论指出其弓法运用具有高度辨识力——在持续低音之间捕捉跳动的杂音，使音色深沉而共鸣强烈。专辑中部分曲目借鉴筝的弹拨方式处理琴弦，并引入木质的吱嘎声、敲击与喉音般的低吼，拓展了大提琴的声响边界。另一些曲目则将大提琴转化为打击乐器或巨大的共振腔体，呈现非十二平均律的螺旋式结构，声响如金属薄板在混凝土洞穴中被演奏。整体风格与Fred Frith的吉他独奏、Hans Reichel的实验创作路径相近，既具前卫探索性，又保留可听的音乐性。

items.body:
Thee most coveted collection of Coil demos surfaces on CD, opening a window onto the recording sessions for their pivotal 1991 release, ‘Love’s Secret Domain’. 

Originally collated on a demo tape for WaxTrax! records in 1989 under the working title ‘The Side Effects of Life’, these are the raw early iterations of tracks that would become ‘Love’s Secret Domain’, and arguably one of the ’90s definitive albums. Only a handful of the original cassette are known to exist, and have understandably become important artefacts in their own right, so it’s a massive buzz to finally, physically grasp the album in its entirety, here supplemented by material off the ‘Wrong Eye/Scope’ 7”.

Between the album’s two bookending versions of ‘Fidgit’, which later appeared on the ‘WaxTrax! Sampler #2’ tape in 1989, the album spools familiar yet rawer examples of Coil classics such as ‘Dark River’, ‘Teenage Lightening’ and ‘Love's Secret Domain’, each replete with haphazard fades, cuts and stereo bias, and often with lots of ferric noise. However none of that should put prospective listeners off, with results more faithful to the original than the weirdly pitched version found on YouTube and p2p sites.   

Ultimately it’s a proper find for Coil diehards, but anyone intrigued by the hidden reverse of what was going on in parallel to Rave, grunge and post rock in the phase shift between later ‘80s and early ‘90s, should fill their boots.
items._cn_summary: 这张合集收录了Coil为1991年关键专辑《Love's Secret Domain》所做的早期原始demo，原为1989年送交WaxTrax!唱片公司的样带，以《The Side Effects of Life》为暂定名。专辑中包含两首首尾呼应的'Fidgit'版本，以及'Dark River''Teenage Lightening''Love's Secret Domain'等曲目的粗糙早期形态，保留了随意的淡出、剪切与立体声偏移以及大量磁带底噪。相较于流传于网络的音调失真版本，这些录音更接近原始意图，对乐迷而言是罕见的实物档案。整体展现了Coil在80年代末至90年代初，与锐舞、垃圾摇滚、后摇平行发展的暗潮实验脉络，融合工业电子与氛围建构，声音设计极具先锋性与探索价值。

items.body:
One of the UK’s most distinctive filmmakers returns to the sea, replete with his original synth score - as on ‘Bait’ and ‘Enys Men’ - but notably damper, deeply blue; surely evoking fellow Cornish native AFX’s ‘SAW II’, BoC interluuds, Mordant Music, classic folk horror OSTs.

Centred around the tale of a trawler that returns, sans crew, to a Cornish harbour years after it was thought lost, ‘The Rose Of Nevada’ typically draws on what Mark Jenkin knows best - the people, places and metaphysics of the Atlantic peninsula - whilst ideally emphasising the atmosphere with his special ingredient score. His palette of tape-smudged analog synths feels especially washed out and suggestive of his subject in its briny tone and oceanic scale, which evidently works a treat as a discrete work in its own right, severed from imagery. 

There’s possibly a Kernewek word for “hiraeth”, or “sehnsucht” - a sense of longing, nostalgia - that we’re not aware of, but may perfectly fit the feeling of Jenkin’s music here. Sea-legged loops and sustained drones colour the air with a palpable melancholy in passage from the bittersweet tang of ‘Kneebone Barton’, as used on the trailer, and throughout the album’s patches of decaying wheeze, staining the surface like rust or efflorescence on weathered coves. 

And in the day-dreamiest sense it all fades in/out of consciousness with a perfectly ghostly wow and flutter, as leaching from ‘Through The Gaps’ parts into the slurred whorl of ‘What’s Your Name,’ ephemeral concrète of ‘Look At It’, and final folksy shuffle off into the horizon with ‘Rose of Nevada.’ Here’s looking forward to the film.

items._cn_summary: Mark Jenkin 为电影《The Rose Of Nevada》创作的原声配乐，是一部以磁带质感模拟合成器为核心的氛围作品。整张专辑围绕康沃尔海岸的海洋意象展开，采用模糊、褪色的模拟合成器音色，营造出类似AFX《SAW II》、BoC 中段以及经典民间恐怖片配乐的潮湿蓝色质感。音乐以循环乐句与持续低音为主，在咸涩的音调中透露出强烈的怀旧与乡愁。曲目之间通过幽灵般的抖颤与渐隐渐现自然衔接，从开篇的苦乐交织到结尾的民谣式散场，形成统一的海洋叙事。作为独立于影像的独立作品，这张专辑凭借其独到的声音设计与地域文化意象，呈现出浓烈的实验氛围美学。

items.body:
Stefan Betke aka Pole’s hugely influential debut LP of frayed dub experiments resurfaces for a 20th anniversary reissue, taking us back to smoked out nights at the turn of the century and some of the finest post basic-channel dub echoes ever released. Essential listening if you’re into anything from Rhythm & Sound to Vainqueur, Jon Hassell to Jackie Mittoo.

As legend goes, Pole took his name from a malfunctioning Waldorf 4-Pole filter which produced hisses and pops which weren’t really controllable or predictable, much like a living organism. Betke realised the potential and came to alchemically morph and render them with judicious FX dubbing into a groundbreaking sort of minimalist electro-dub that sounds exceedingly good with a spliff and glass of booze. Working somewhere between the variants of abstract techno on Chain Reaction and Mille Plateaux’s cutting edge minimalist strains, Pole’s first trio of albums inarguably helped lay the foundations for dub techno as it’s come to be known and are held in the highest regard by practically everyone who owns them. 

The Pole aesthetic is patently laid out in ‘1’, where his organic clicks ’n pops come out to play accompanied by lilting organ and jazzy bass channelling Jackie Mittoo via Jon Hassell and Rhythm & Sound into a uniquely, gauzy, gaseous state.  So strong was the impact of the album on the late ‘90s underground, they even generated a “pastiche” that was unwittingly issued (and subsequently deleted) by Fat Cat on their split series, but was purportedly made by V/Vm in a snidey but frankly hilarious prank, albeit one that demonstrates just how ubiquitous and influential Betke’s sound was at the time. More than that, it’s fair to say the 20 year cycle hasn’t rinsed out the appeal of this triptych one bit; it remains one of electronic music’s most enigmatic and strangely moving, tactile bodies of work.
items._genre: dub techno / minimal electronic / experimental dub
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Pole（Stefan Betke）的首张长专辑20周年再版。创作源自一台故障的Waldorf四极滤波器产生的不可控嘶响与爆破声，他将这种机械故障当作有机生命体来对待，通过精细的延迟与混响效果处理，将其转化为极简的电子dub声响。音乐运作于Chain Reaction的抽象techno与Mille Plateaux前沿极简主义之间，爵士化的低音线与管风琴漂浮在沙砾般的电子噪声之上，呈现出朦胧而气态的质感。这套三连作在九十年代末地下场景中影响深远，曾被V/Vm以恶搞方式仿制发行，足见其声音的辨识度与渗透力。二十年后再听，这套作品依然保持着独特的触感和难以言说的感染力。

items.body:
Barcelona-based Argentine sound artist Dima uses mythology to re-examine her personal world on 'Salva', dissolving instrumental phrases with confounding granular processes and allowing fragile trip-hop-inspired songs to emerge from the ambiance.

There's an unexpected balance on 'Salva'. At first, on the opener 'SOELAR' or its breathy follow-up 'APOGEO', you might think you have it figured out, its atmospheric blend of plasticky flutes and sci-fi pads. But as the latter track hits its third act, something unexpected appears - Dima's voice was already there, haunting the soundscape, but when a slowed-down beat joins it provides a real surprise. And 'Salva' keeps rocking from side to side, never settling into a reliable groove. On 'QUANTUM', Dima sings into an echoing void almost unaccompanied, but on 'FOLDING INWARD', she adds atmospheric synths and gong-y resonances to go in another direction, moving away from song structure towards grim abstraction. 

And after the one-two punch of the album's poppiest tracks, 'REACH' and 'IT HAD TO BURN', Dima concludes with 'Inked', a throbbing dark ambient nightmare that seems to dive deep beneath an alien ocean. Terrifying stuff.
items._genre: experimental electronic / dark ambient / glitch / trip-hop / vocal abstraction
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷声音艺术家Dima以神话视角重审个人世界，将器乐乐句溶解于颗粒合成处理之中，让脆弱的trip-hop风格歌曲从环境音中浮现。专辑始终维持着出人意料的平衡感：开场曲目以塑料质长笛与科幻合成器垫音构建氛围，随后人声早已潜伏于声景之中，直至减速节拍加入才带来惊喜。作品拒绝落入固定律动，时而近乎无伴奏地唱入回声虚空，时而转向抽象化处理，远离歌曲结构。终曲以深潜入异星海洋的暗潮噩梦收束，节拍阴郁而具有压迫感。整体展现出声音设计的层次感与叙事张力，是融合人声、颗粒合成与暗潮氛围的实验性作品。

The specially packaged slab
items.body:
Steel-forged industrial brutalism from the Brum blast furnace of HALT, earning their Downwards stripes with a label debut that revels in dread tension and Midlands gloom somewhere between Scorn, Antonym, Karl O’Connor.

‘Slag Anthems’ cements Nathan Shwalbe & Craig Earp’s duo to the Downwards firm after Regis summoned them to the label’s 30th anniversary show at Birmingham’s Central, hosted amid familiar rogues; Surgeon, Russell Haswell, Mick Harris, Antonym and more. The specially packaged slab of heck builds on the solid foundations of 2020’s ‘Memory Fields’ LP for Erbium Records with a concentrated show of strength oozing from emulsified subs to plangent brutalist sound architecture, largely avoiding any regular drum patterns in favour of hulking offbeat structures and hallucinatory spectral silhouettes.

The duo’s native Brum is a presence and aesthetic muse throughout, prompting them to clash bin lids like duelling scimitars over pure bass effluence on ’Sassenach’, and lace their thrumming subs with a shiver of melodic glory on ‘Black Car’, or pull it all right down into Scorn-type mire on the recoiling drum play of ‘Rift Cantata’. A certain atmospheric levity to ‘Chernozem’ keeps it teetering just above an abyss they toe with macabre alacrity on ‘Pillars’, playing to a balance of black humour and uncompromising grit they tuck where the sun don’t shine on ‘I was just pleased to see you’.

Heavy.
items._cn_summary: HALT由Nathan Shwalbe与Craig Earp组成，这张专辑是他们在Downwards厂牌的首发作品，延续了2020年Erbium Records发行的'Memory Fields'的路线。整张专辑几乎回避常规鼓点节奏，转而以庞大而笨重的离拍结构和迷幻的频谱轮廓构建声响。伯明翰的工业城市气质贯穿始终，低频饱满浑厚，呈现出粗粝的暴力主义美学。作品融合了Scorn式的黏稠泥沼、Karl O'Connor的冷峻张力以及Antonym的阴郁氛围，在深渊与黑色幽默之间寻找平衡。部分曲目如'Black Car'在厚重的低频之上闪现旋律光芒，'Pillow'则以诡异姿态逼近深渊边缘，展现了乐队在工业框架内对声音层次与情绪张力的精细把控。

Fully transcendent material - essential listening for fans of Alice Coltrane, Jon Hassell, Sun Ra, Sons of Kemet, Dorothy Ashby, Laraaji. items.body:
London-based "ambient jazz" ace Nala Sinephro steps up her game on 'Endlessness', playfully zig-zagging around an electrifying continuous arpeggio over ten cosmically interlinked tracks assembling decades of spiritual jazz echoing down the line. Fully transcendent material - essential listening for fans of Alice Coltrane, Jon Hassell, Sun Ra, Sons of Kemet, Dorothy Ashby, Laraaji.

It's Sinephro's boundless ambition that bubbles to the surface on 'Endlessness'. She was ever so subtly bold on her debut 'Space 1.8', sensing out a connection between ecstatic ambient music and contemporary jazz that unfolded with gentle, measured charm. Here, she lets her imagination run wild, weaving her historical narrative with vivid, lively threads from across the musical spectrum. Jazz, specifically the spiritual strain that Coltrane, Sanders et al cultivated in the '60s, forms the album's musical backbone, and Sinephro jumps off from that point, infusing familiar tempos with lush modular electronics, uncompromising angular rhythms and sparkling orchestral flourishes. Like Sun Ra's most mischievous work, it's music that betrays a voracious appetite for hierarchy-free admiration - Sinephro is clearly a literate listener, and her passion for sounds as they stretch across borders is palpable from the beginning.

So how might you connect such a wide litany if inspirations? Sinephro opts to balance her energy with a single arpeggio that runs throughout the entire album, using its relative stasis to provoke considerations about the album's central theme. If the concept  is a way to show how the composer-performer is able to add new ingredients to an established form, Sinephro follows the concept aesthetically, refreshing her mode constantly while retaining a recognisable sonic through-line. Her inspiration is "life cycles and rebirth", and from track to track, she reconfigures the logic of a single core idea. 'Continuum 1' sets the initial pace with a waterfall of evolving bleeps and delicate harp chimes; fidgety drums and muted horns follow to help cast our mind through jazz history, but Sinephro doesn't let the track stagnate for a moment. In the middle section, glossy cinematic strings - provided by Orchestrate’s 21 players - intertwine with Sinephro's woozy synths and Morgan Simpson's 'On The Corner'-inspired tempo-fluxing rhythms and we're transported into a different realm entirely.

The hyperactivity continues on 'Continuum 2' as Sinephro obscures the root arpeggio in a verdant tangle of piano, horn and precise percussion that's queered by her giddy psychoacoustic processes. And the mood shifts completely when we reach the gorgeous 'Continuum 3'; Sinephro's arpeggio is hushed to a lullaby-like sine wave crawl that's woken up by her lively harp improvisations. Soon, she interrupts the mood with fusion-era synth jabs, bringing the orchestra back to add some cautious schmaltz that's repeatedly challenged - most obviously on 'Continuum 5', a brief interlude that sounds like Wendy Carlos vs. Blue Note. And when we hit the album's first big interlude, 'Continuum 6', it's a payoff that brings Sinephro's parallel universes together, coddling her hard-panned oscillations with brittle, upfront beats and Sam Gendel-like pitch-bent swoons. Study a little closer, and there are fireworks in even the album's most delicate moments: 'Continuum 8' is a clear highlight that distorts the album's logic with R&B smooveness, and 'Continuum 9', a rare (almost) drumless composition, cements Sinephro's commitment to early electronic music, pushing her synths into the foreground as the album waltzes to its conclusion.

On the finale, Sinephro fires every musical synapse, turning her arpeggio into swooping runs that duck and dive across itchy beats and Alice Coltrane-like ecstatic synth solos, and as it comes to a close, the chaos is calmed with a muted piano that's tape-fluttered until it gasps a final breath. Remarkable music.
items._genre: ambient jazz / spiritual jazz / electronic / modular synth / harp
items._cn_summary: Nala Sinephro 的第二张专辑以一条贯穿全作的持续琶音为核心线索，将六十年代精神爵士的血脉与模块化电子、不妥协的棱角节奏以及管弦乐配器编织在一起。专辑共十首相互关联的曲目，主题围绕生命循环与重生，每首作品对核心琶音进行重新配置——从瀑布般演化的电子声响与竖琴，到迷幻声学处理下的钢琴铜管组合，再到被管弦乐小心翼翼包裹的摇篮曲式正弦波爬行。乐手 Morgan Simpson 提供受 Miles Davis 'On The Corner' 启发的节拍律动，Orchestrate 的二十一位乐手贡献了光泽的电影化弦乐层次。Sinephro 在首作中展现的克制与微妙在此被放大为更狂野的想象力，音乐呈现出对跨越边界的听觉方式的贪婪胃口。

items.body:
Catholics Against Architecture release "Columns" via Fourth Dimension.

"Catholics Against Architecture is the name Chris Connelly has given this project that here collects twelve songs crafted from sonic collages, spoken word, fractured melodies, vocals not far removed from those that David Bowie traded some of his best songs on, rivulets of subdued noise and seemingly random location recordings, tender guitar work, tape manipulation and all kinds of other sounds either in between or beyond. Together, these compositions sit outside convention and pay little regard to whatever the so-called zeitgeist may or may not happen to be. If anything, they draw from his own wonderfully rich past, beginning with his co-founding of avant-garde post-punk outfit Finitribe and moving on through his involvement with Revolting Cocks and various other Al Jourgensen-helmed groups before joining Martin Atkins’ ambitious Pigface project and then more or less operating as an artist under his own name. In the decades since he began his artistic career in the early ’80s, he has maintained this experimental disposition while embracing everything from art-pop and rock to the industrial noise he first cut his teeth on. To place him in a comfortable box would do nothing but serve his defiant temperament some kind of injustice.

“Columns” is no exception. It’s an album that incorporates many ideas and keeps moving while still somehow magically adding up to a whole that gels and seems to make perfect sense. From its occasionally lo-fi stature (due to being recorded on antiquated reel to reel and various cassette players in a state of disrepair) to its jittery blend of free jazz, tone poetry, labyrinthine textural currents and found sounds, passages of hiss and mature songcraft, it points to an artist perfectly at ease with his position as somebody capable of juggling many ideas. Thematically bound to an anti-religion stance which makes sense in these especially turbulent times where rampant polarisation is galvanised by religion as well as politics, “Columns” stands as a testament to something that can never be compounded enough. The title itself, replete with ironic quotation marks, subtly refers to the columns found within churches as well as the columns of smoke generated by religious war.

Ultimately, the album witnesses an artist continuing to explore new trajectories, further prod at ideas that perhaps already presented themselves, and remain true to his place as someone far more than the sum of his parts."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Chris Connelly主导的实验项目Catholics Against Architecture发行，收录十二首以声音拼贴、念白、破碎旋律、磁带操控与即兴噪音为核心的作品。Connelly自八十年代初参与Finitribe、Revolting Cocks、Pigface等项目以来，始终坚持跨领域探索，从工业噪音到艺术流行均有涉猎。本作延续其一贯的反叛姿态，融合自由爵士、诗歌体吟诵、迷宫式织体与现成音响，使用老式开盘机和卡带机录制，呈现出粗粝的质感。主题上以反宗教为基调，标题暗指教堂立柱与宗教战争烟柱的双重意象，与当下日益极化的社会语境形成呼应。整体构思路径清晰却不拘一格，作品之间松散而有机地构成统一整体。

Following the commercial success of their singles "It's My Life", "Life's What You Make It” and album "The Colour of Spring”, Talk Talk retreated into the shado
items.body:
One of the most influential, insular and multi-layered albums of the last five decades, created through endless hours of improvisation - involving almost fifty musicians and recorded in complete darkness, 'Spirit Of Eden' was a radical departure for Talk Talk, ' an album that has attained almost mythical status since its release in 1988.

Following the commercial success of their singles "It's My Life", "Life's What You Make It” and album "The Colour of Spring”, Talk Talk retreated into the shadows and produced an album that still defies categorisation. Mark Hollis is said to have demanded the players record in almost complete darkness, improvising for hours to produce individual parts without hearing any backing tracks or surrounding material.

"Spirit Of Eden" is one of the most fearless and rewarding leaps a commercially successful band has ever taken, and continues to cast its influence almost 40 years later.
items._genre: experimental rock / post-rock / improvisation / art rock
items._cn_summary: Talk Talk 在1988年商业巅峰后彻底转型，摒弃传统录音流程，将近五十位乐手置于近乎全黑的环境中长时间即兴演奏，不设参考音轨、不设固定结构，所有声部在黑暗中独立生成后被编织在一起。这种创作方式彻底脱离了流行摇滚的制作逻辑，将唱片从产品变为事件。专辑横跨氛围、爵士即兴、简约古典与另类摇滚之间，至今仍难以被归入任何现成类型。其影响力持续辐射至后摇、慢核、实验民谣等领域，被视为商业乐队所能做出的最勇敢跳跃之一。黑胶重刻版本保留了原始混音的动态与呼吸感，适合以整段时间沉浸聆听。
