items.body: If a tree falls in the forest, does it make a sound? And what if an entire forest falls? Around Here, The Birds Plant The Trees, inspired by a “clear-felled wasteland” in Leitrim, Ireland, amplifies these questions. In the digital era, it prompts an additional question: “When the liner notes are integral to the release, will listeners intuit the point?” We hope so, in the same manner as those hearing classical works over the centuries have gleaned the intentions of the composers, from “The Goldfinch” to The Four Seasons. In her first work for ensemble, Natalia Beylis uses different instruments to evoke “the rustle of beetles in the hedgerow, the squeak of a leaning Sitka spruce, a lone curlew’s call,” and her overall concern is that listeners will hear the richness of a richness of a landscape and be moved to protect it. While this landscape is incredibly specific: a single field on 12 December 2025, beginning at 6 a.m. ~ it could be any environment threatened by large multinational corporations, who swoop in to offer short-term recompense for long-term loss. Looking out over the field, Beylis notes the activity of a single blackbird, and later, an entire flock. Adding to the pathos is the fact that even birds are now endangered (for details, we recommend Robert Macfarlane & Jackie Morris’ The Book of Birds). If the music of the actual birds is inadequate to promote empathy, might music take up the cause? The alternative is to say nothing and to play nothing. As one might expect, the 51-minute piece is filled with intricate description and high drama. The cello’s low notes launch the piece in a reverent tone, considering at a field that once was a forest. As the other members of the string quartet join in, the nuance starts to develop. What began as drone becomes a harmonic suite with a distinctly Irish lilt. Then the first taps of percussion, like small creatures rustling through the grass, foraging for breakfast. A period of abstraction follows, during which every resident of field and forest receives their own spotlight. The blackbird eats and mates and cross-pollinates. The squirrels rush to and fro; the fox chases the shrew. All the while, the breeze threads through the branches of the hawthorn, creating a rhythm of leaves. The atmosphere seems peaceful until the thrums of the 15th minute, a soupçon of danger as most of the animals and instruments go into hiding. The contrast between presence and absence is integral to the composition. One feels the recession of sound as one might feel the destruction of trees. What was once lush becomes a hush, like the quietude of midday. Then the drone re-develops, a symbol of hope and regrowth. A vast cymbal strike like a gong at 32:07 interrupts the process, leaving only the drums and the wind in its wake. Willie Stewart’s work in this segment is enthralling; it sounds like architecture being built. But as the strings re-enter, are they busy as bees or as bulldozers? The listener is left to decide. Beylis initially planned to “write something to equal the harsh cacophony of the harvesting machines as they shred the nests of fledgling buzzards; to evoke the rumbling shaking noise I’d hear in bed at night as they crashed the huge trees they’d cut to the ground,” but relented for the sake of the blackbird. The dissonance that follows the drums suggests that the idea was not totally discarded. This makes the closing segment all the sweeter: consonance rising out of dissonance, form from chaos. The forest may have been leveled, but around here, the birds plant the trees. This being said, the story is not meant to encourage as much as it is to unsettle. Robert Plant once sang, “if there’s a bustle in your hedgerow, don’t be alarmed now.” Beylis has a different message: be alarmed. Be very alarmed. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: contemporary classical / string quartet / field-inspired composition / ambient / experimental
items._cn_summary: Natalia Beylis 首部室内乐作品，灵感来自爱尔兰 Leitrim 一片被皆伐后的荒地。整部作品以弦乐四重奏为核心，加入打击乐，捕捉自然声响与生态叙事。从大提琴低沉的持续音出发，逐步发展为带爱尔兰风味的和声组曲，辅以模拟甲虫在树篱中窸窣、云杉吱鸣、麻鹬孤鸣的声音。作品既描绘黑鹂觅食、松鼠奔窜、狐狸追捕鼩鼱的生动场景，也通过第15分钟的低频震荡暗示危险降临，动物与乐器一同隐匿。32分07秒的钹击如同洪钟，象征毁灭与重生之间循环往复的进程。乐评特别提及 Willie Stewart 的打击乐段落，建筑感般的层次建构令人着迷。

items.body:
Effortlessly easy on the ear and yet still somehow fathoms-deep, Tara Clerkin Trio’s latest is their most refined and fully-formed transmission yet, mining a precious sweetspot between chamber-jazz, Plone-style bric-a-brac electronics, Crescent’s lo-fi reveries and the urban pressure of the Young Echo collective, unpicking decades of British musical history in the process. Trust, it’s a special one.

Like every great band, TCT know their history. They've grown up with and formed their identity in the shadow of Bristol's musical lore, whether it's The Pop Group, Massive Attack or Flying Saucer Attack, and when they use traceable elements, it feels like a believable part of their DNA. Thankfully, they meaningfully add to that narrative too, not adapting an aesthetic for easy consumption. Part of this might be down to their makeup; they formed in the late 20-teens from the ashes of the Tara Clerkin Band, a larger ensemble that Clerkin had put together to expand the scope of her folk-y pop compositions. And when most of the members moved on, stepbrothers Sunny-Joe Paradiso and Patrick Benjamin stuck around to see where the road might lead. All "proper" players, they've traditionally let their songs appear from what sounds like loose, casual improvisations, like you're tuned into Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society' band running through Laika's 'Silver Apples of the Moon'.

So you get a song like the brilliant 'Ups & Downs', that simmers for a good four minutes with wheezing harmonium, double bass and clarinet, percussion just rumbling in the background somewhere, before a jerky sampled beat, Mellotron strings and Clerkin's voice would have you thinking Matt Elliott's behind the boards. But 'Somewhere Good' is also remarkably tight when it needs to be, walking a tightrope between easy breezy and meticulous with acrobatic skill. Opener 'Lake Walk', for example, sounds intentionally naive, jammed out loosely on synthesised and real woodwind that's caught in a vortex of Space Echo, before 'Lazy Daisy' cuts it short with its more ordered (but still kinda slouchy) beat-heavy dreampop atmosphere. It's where the album's shape really coagulates, between Broadcast's dramatic early EPs (back when they were touring with Plone) and Pram's best shit, just lightly tweezed at the edges, its creases relaxed to fit in with Laila Sakini's quietly genius 'Paloma'. And that mood carries the record even when Clerkin's voice - pursed into a soulful croon or a lackadaisical murmur - vanishes completely. One of the most gripping moments arrives with 'There Was a Nice Sunset', effortlessly matching slowcore drums with piano flourishes and synths, locking into the same general feeling but widening the boundaries, nodding to Adrian Sherwood's lysergic work on Creation Rebel's 'Starship Africa'. 

There's years of British musical history baked into this stuff, and yet it feels wholly new.
items._genre: chamber jazz / lo-fi electronics / dream pop / experimental folk
items._cn_summary: Tara Clerkin Trio的第三张专辑在室内爵士、拼贴电子、lo-fi梦幻流行之间找到了精准的平衡点。乐评指出乐队从布里斯托丰富的音乐传统中汲取养分——从The Pop Group到Flying Saucer Attack——但并非简单挪用美学，而是将碎片化的即兴创作与传统乐器演奏融为一炉。手风琴、低音提琴、单簧管与采样节拍、合成器木管、Mellotron弦乐交织，营造出松散而有机的氛围。专辑在随性与精密之间走钢丝，歌曲从缓慢酝酿的即兴段落过渡到结构化的梦幻流行，Clerkin的嗓音时而深沉时而懒散地游走于器乐层之间。整张作品承载了数十年英国音乐史的积淀，却呈现出全然新颖的面貌，是一次兼具历史纵深与当下感的成熟创作。

items.body:
Dean Blunt’s totemic, genre-agnostic first ’Black Metal’ album is back in circulation on the heels of its killer 2nd volume, singing out a singular sort of mid-decade London blooz where his myriad circles run into one.

In 2014 ‘Black Metal’ arrived as Blunt’s 4th solo album in a string of quietly groundbreaking and guess-again solo recordings following the break-up of Hype Williams, his duo with Inga Copeland. It was an instant fave, raved about everywhere, and with the benefit of hindsight is arguably one of the past decade’s definitive highlights; a record symptomatic of the way staid generic borders were dissolving, expressing a lucid but woozy pathos that still feels timeless, yet very much of its flat-time, when the stream of musical history had pooled into the reservoir of the internet.

Returning to its slow baked charms years later ‘Black Metal’ has lost none of its allure, with a reflective stillness still belying its depths. Nimbly joining wipe clean presets and crisp licks of original instrumentation with vocals by Blunt and regular spar Joanne Robertson, their baker’s dozen tunes somehow consolidate aspects of everything from hip hop to chamber music, indie-pop to R&B with experimental wit and ohrwurming magick that places it among his most memorable and surprising records.

From the symphonic Americana lilt of ‘Lush’ to its amazing 13 minute centrepiece of chamber soul gauze ‘Forever’ and the free jazz meets folk and roadrap synthscape of ‘Grade’ it coolly piques curiosity and perplexes from every angle, resolving unfamiliar styles with a pop-sharpened manner that follows a path first taken by A.R. Kane and which quite possibly ignited a reappraisal of the problematic way in which Black music has been perceived and categorised in popular/critical culture.

All time business = unmissable.
items._genre: experimental / genre-blending / chamber soul / lo-fi / abstract pop
items._cn_summary: Dean Blunt 的首张《Black Metal》专辑横跨嘻哈、室乐、独立流行与R&B，将预设音色与原始乐器录音交织，配合他与 Joanne Robertson 松弛的人声，呈现一种清醒却朦胧的忧伤气质。十三首曲目风格跨度极大，从交响化的美式民谣《Lush》，到十三分钟室内灵魂氛围之作《Forever》，再到自由爵士、民谣与路说唱合成器景观交汇的《Grade》，几乎在每个角度都制造意外的听觉转折。整张专辑流淌着解构类型边界的实验直觉，在流行旋律骨架上嫁接实验性的声响碎片，既保留了顺耳的钩子，又始终拒绝落入任何常规分类。这种跨类型整合方式让人联想到 A.R. Kane 对黑人音乐再评估的路径，也在某种意义上重新打开了英国另类音乐的可能性。

items.body:
Not the birth of acid house, but a thrilling piece of synth raga set to brisk disco beats, Bollywood soundtrack composer Charanjit Singh’s ’82 LP is simply a landmark in its own right, and a proper ‘floor-filler to boot.

Since its first reissue in 2010, Singh’s cult, early use of the TB-303 on driving machine beats has been erroneously hailed the birth of acid house. OK the formula is there, but Chris Carter’s ‘Spaces Between’ (1980) and his CTI jam ‘Dancing Ghosts’ got there a couple of years before Singh, at the very least, and neither really inform the genius of Phuture and co a few years later. In any event, ‘Synthesizing: Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’ is just an incredibly fruity boost to any club, revolving 10 hypnotic, pulsating jams closer to early Irdial (say, Aqua Regia’s ‘Hot Love’) than owt from the Chi. 

Taking a minute away from knocking out Bollywood scores and leading his wedding band covering popular songs, Singh would land upon a stroke of genius with ‘Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’, finding the sweetspot between prevailing hi-NRG disco and millennia of raga traditions that patently transcended the sum of their parts more than 40 years later. It sounds very much of its time, rather than the stripped back linearity of later acid house, evidenced in the florid keyboard urges of ‘Raga Bhupali’, transposing a steamy sort of club canter to somewhere even more humid.

A real club evergreen, suck it and see.
items._genre: synth raga / electronic / world fusion / disco
items._cn_summary: 1982年宝莱坞作曲家Charanjit Singh录制了这张极具前瞻性的专辑，将TB-303合成器节拍与传统印度拉格旋律融合，创造出十首催眠般脉动的舞曲作品。乐评指出，虽常被误认为是酸屋音乐的起源，但实际更接近早期Irdial厂牌那种实验性电子舞曲气质。专辑巧妙地在当时盛行的Hi-NRG迪斯科节奏与千年拉格传统之间找到平衡点，各首曲目如'Raga Bhupali'以繁复的键盘线条呈现，将俱乐部律动推向更为湿热的氛围。作为融合东西方音乐语言的里程碑之作，其文化与音乐双重层面的开创性使其在四十年后依然散发独特魅力，适合寻求跨文化电子音乐的听众深入聆听。

items.body:
The crème de la crème of Gallic dubbers - Full Circle, Froid Dub, Krikor, and Shelter - tactfully diffuse the heady tekkerz of ‘80s French “ethno-industrial” legends Vox Populi!, whose catalogue of wonders continues to inspire wayward musicks...

If it wasn’t obvious from the titles of their 1987 classic ‘Half Dead Ganja Music’ (as reissued by big fan, Spencer Clark in 2013), or from the louche looseness of 1986’s ‘Sucre De Pastèque’ (recently reissued by Dark Entries), Axel Kyrou’s cult unit Vox Populi! were partial to a zoot or two, and their music sounds ideal under the influence. 

Emotional Response task four of VP!’s roughly spiritual descendants to redress their music in a dubwise slipstream of style & pattern; stretching out from Alexis Le Tan & Joakim’s modal, early ‘90s-like Sannyacid Dub on the cusp of ‘Windowpane’-era Coil or The Orb, while Froid Dub bathe ‘Jube Man’ in a deep digidub recalling Sheriff Lindo oddities.

Pivotal Parisian producer Krikor follows in a vein of turbo-charged steppas from his Youth 7” to really send ‘Zen-Dub’ stratospheric, shades away from Element or TNT Roots, and Shelter reduces ‘Micro Climac’ to bubbling residue in step with his works for Séance centre and Emotional Response’s ‘’Checkmate in Dub’ session.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是一次对法国八十年代"民族工业"先驱 Vox Populi! 作品的重塑演绎，由四组当代制作人各自以 dub 美学进行再创作。Full Circle 以近似早期九零年代的迷幻酸性 dub 手法延展原作；Froid Dub 在深沉数字 dub 框架中营造冥想氛围；Krikor 带来高速 steppas 律动，将原曲推向更高能量层级；Shelter 则将声音分解为细碎泡沫般的残响纹理。每位制作人从不同角度切入 dub 的空间纵深与回声结构，既保留了原作的迷幻与异域气质，又赋予其全新的电子化解读。这是一张介于考古与重构之间的混音合集，展现了地下 dub 制作场景对前辈遗产的创造性继承。

items.body:
Pushing back against "Acid Nostalgia", Lawrence English dreams of a moonlit future on 'The Rest is My Ghost', bringing in assistance from a heap of collaborators, including Mats Gustafsson, Tony Buck, Chris Abrahams, Rully Shabara, Norman Westberg and Lena Ito.

Having fully deconstructed his persona on 2022's 'Approach', looking back to his formative influences - William Gibson's 'Neuromancer' and Yoshihisa Tagami's sci-fi manga 'Grey' - English was left with a conundrum that he solved by taking a step back. Last year's 'Even the Horizon Knows its Bounds' was billed as a grand collaborative effort, performed by a litany of English's associates and imagined as an "atmospheric tint" for the Naala Badu building at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. 'The Rest is My Ghost' is very different; more radical and more overtly political than its predecessors, more in line with 2014's charged 'Wilderness of Mirrors' and its brilliant follow-up 'Cruel Optimism', the album takes aim at the contemporary obsession with nostalgia. Provoked by a conversation with Adam Curtis and driven by texts from Mark Fisher, JG Ballard, Katsuhiro Otomo, Franco Berardi, Kate Crawford and Alexie Yurchak and cultural architectural realities like the loss of Los Angeles' signature street lamps and Japan's Metabolists, English searches for a "political projection of nostalgia" that he can subsequently rupture. "Like acid poured onto a surface," he writes. "this use of nostalgia seeks to erode and smooth out the complexity and texture of lived connection and longing, which has until recently guided contemplations of nostalgia."

He's talking about the difference between dreaming of your own past and being sold a neatly packaged pseudo-reality, its highs and lows removed to ease the ingestion. Nobody would argue that 'Stranger Things', for example, wasn't nostalgic, but is its high concept fun comparable with any of its direct influences? Even its soundtrack pales alongside pretty standard straight-to-VHS fodder of the era, it's just cleaner, zippier and more shareable. And the more it dragged on, the less vital it became - a Gen X-core soap opera with eerily familiar visual cues. To represent this concept musically, English moves away from the dense distortions you might expect and instead collects up instrumental performances from a wide swathe of players. But perusing the personnel list and projecting your expectations on the material is part of the process. English obscures everything very purposefully, shrouding the instrumentation in reverb and midnight gusts. If seeing names like Swans' Thor Harris and pedal steel player Chuck Johnson gives you pause, that's the point. English engages in his own hauntological process, extracting the essence from the stems and imprinting it on his soundscapes. He's not eroding the material by any means, but searching out the triggers that play on the imagination, inspiring futures that have never been more difficult to grasp.

And if it sounds dark, it's really not supposed to. Listen through the nocturnal hums and gentle, thrumming ambiance and you'll discover more than you bargained for - even a glimmer of hope. The result is a record that lands somewhere between Les Disques du Crépuscule's post-classical gear, Eno's fourth world experiments with John Hassell and Alan Lamb's influential sound art.
items._genre: experimental / dark ambient / drone / post-rock / hauntology
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚声音艺术家Lawrence English延续其解构个人声学身份的脉络，召集包括Mats Gustafsson、Chris Abrahams、Norman Westberg在内的多位跨领域乐手，以集体演奏为素材构建幽暗音景。专辑对应当代文化中怀旧情绪的商品化与简化，将酸液般的腐蚀性隐喻转化为声响处理：每位合作者的乐器轨迹被厚重混响与午夜气流般的质感笼罩，刻意的模糊化处理构成一种'幽灵学'过程，剥离原奏细节而提取触发想象的本质记忆。文本灵感横跨Mark Fisher、JG Ballard、Franco Berardi等人的政治哲学写作，以及洛杉矶街灯被拆除、 일본新陈代谢派建筑消亡等城市肌理丧失议题。作品摒弃密集失真，转而追求在辽阔混响空间中让合作者演奏痕迹若隐若现，以此对抗被包装成可消费怀旧商品的伪现实，并试图投射难以企及的未来想象。

items.body:
Compiling rare-as-hen's-teeth material from iconic Aotearoa/New Zealand label World Resources, 'Fully Nowhere' presents four sides of scuzzy lo-fi rock, drone, noise pop and improv from a tight cadre of the country's most prolific outsiders.

Established in the 1990s in Wellington, World Resources was a DIY label that specialised in tapes and micro-edition lathe-cut 7" singles and the home of Donald Smith, Paul Toohey and Tony McGurk's long-running free noise/drone band Surface of the Earth. It's an imprint that helped impact its region's knottiest outsider surges, so World of Echo does us a favor here by scraping together some of its rarest and most enduring sides, assembling a 25-track collection of some of the best basement drone and most surreal noise pop that's ever emerged from the Southern Hemisphere. The anthology begins in 1994 with two 7"s from Gorgecop, a short-lived solo project from Toohey. And already we're in impressive territory, with slashy grot-rock gear that wouldn't be out of place alongside The Shadow Ring and waved kosmische synth experiments that have more in common with the Dusseldorf wave. 

Donald Smith's Lucky Stars project yanks us back down to earth with the surprisingly bright and breezy 'Winter Call' a track that's so deliciously lo-fi that its drum machine beat barely cracks a faint pulse. Side B houses the grimy 'Hospital' and 'Smell of a Man's Room' from McGurk's Sewer solo project, tracks that originally appeared in 1995 on lathe cut of just 20 units that apparently never left his flat, and New Zealand Guitar Orchestra, a collaborative project between Surface of the Earth and Dress, have their two album releases condensed into a long stretch of submerged noise and interference that's worth the asking price alone. Of course, Surface of the Earth have to appear at some point and their track 'Shield' rounds up the side, with the brilliantly faded 'Commandcom' opening the next. Here, the trio's work is contextualized alongside their solo experiments, work as K-Group, Sewer and Destrifan that helps piece together a past, present and future of three DIY icons.
items._genre: lo-fi noise / drone / noise pop / experimental improv
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由World of Echo厂牌发行，梳理了来自新西兰Aotearoa的DIY厂牌World Resources自1990年代以来的稀有录音。合辑收录25首曲目，涵盖lo-fi摇滚、drone、噪音流行与即兴实验，涉及Gorgecop、Lucky Stars、Sewer、New Zealand Guitar Orchestra以及Surface of the Earth等多个项目。其中包括McGurk的Sewer作品原版仅压制20张且从未离开其公寓的lathe cut唱片，以及Surface of the Earth成员各自的solo、K-Group、Destrifan等分支计划。编年史式结构将乐队的过去、现在与未来拼合，呈现南半球地下实验场景中极少见的声音档案。

items.body:
Greek harpist and composer Sissi Rada interprets the music of Richard Wagner and Johannes Brahms with unfathomable levels of detail and charm, resulting in one of the most gorgeously executed records of the year. Trust - it’s fully essential listening FFO Joanna Newsom, Svitlana Nianio, Kate Bush, Delphine Dora, Nikos Mamangakis…​

Sissi Makropoulou has been pinging our radar for a while now, but especially hard since 2024's Stroom-released 'Aporia' and that dazzling ‘Demeter In Aexone’ album that properly locked us in to her brand of uncanny avant dream-folk, a highly distinctive signature sound she developed even further on the fantastic 'Nana Butu' earlier this year. She’s a serial collaborator - with Lena Platonos, Brian Eno, Christina Vantzou, Jay Glass Dubs -  even Lee "Scratch" Perry -  all the while composing chamber music on the side. And It's that latter practice that comes to the fore on ‘Serious Songs’ singing in German while attacking Wagner's chilly 'Fünf Gedichte für eine Frauenstimme' (Five Poems for a Female Voice) on the A side, and Brahms' pious 'Vier ernste Gesänge' (Four Serious Songs) on the flip. As you'd expect, it isn't just a simple recital; with harp and voice the focal points, packed out with winding, nebulous arrangements and perspicacious references to avant-garde musical history, integrating dissonant orchestral elements, prepared piano, opera, classical guitar, environmental sounds and foreboding oscillations  - with an exquisite ear for detail.

Oddly for music this tranquil, it benefits from increased volume - at least a level where you can marvel at the array of tiny, unusual production flourishes. And it's a suite that grows and grows. On 'Wesendonck 1’, she opens with voice and harp recalling Joanna Newsom's folk-inspired song cycle 'Ys'. But as the piece develops, she begins to slowly show her hand, introducing harmonic, hypnotic effects to blur the edges. The result is discombobulating in the best way, sounding as dreamy as Julee Cruise's 'Floating into the Night' while somehow still remaining true to the source material. The drama continues to build on 'Wesendonck 2', her delivery of the words - written by poet Mathilde Wesendonck who Wagner was famously besotted with - fittingly dramatic, assisted by brass and grinding drums broken occasionally by moments of ineffable beauty. On 'Wesendonck 4', Makropoulou augments the production with metallophone chimes, fixing sequences with growling synths and heavily processed cries.

Sissi plays a remarkable sleight of hand on the flip. Beginning conservatively, she introduces Brahms' cycle of Lutheran biblical readings with a celestial harp and a gently experimental vocal, pitch shifted to a screwed conclusion. On 'Brahms 2', her performance is kinked by disorienting concrète-style operatic spools that pull us into another musical timeline entirely. She is so confident with her subject matter - whether it's the classical canon, folk, electronic or neue musik - that it all sounds like a natural extension of her practice, converging into something that fully defies categorisation.

Anyway, words don’t really do it for this one. Just give it a spin and you’ll soon melt into it, one of the most quietly startling albums released this year.
items._cn_summary: 希腊竖琴演奏家Sissi Rada将瓦格纳与勃拉姆斯的经典声乐作品彻底解构重组。专辑以竖琴与人声为核心，融入失谐管弦乐元素、预制钢琴、古典吉他、环境声效与不安的振荡器音色，将古典文本转化为梦境般的前卫民谣空间。A面演绎瓦格纳的《五首女性之歌》，从类似Joanna Newsom的民谣叙事逐渐铺展为催眠的迷幻声响；B面以实验性的天庭竖琴引入勃拉姆斯的《四首严肃的歌》，通过具体音乐式的歌剧碎片将听者拉入另一条音乐时间线。整体呈现出对古典素材的高度个性化再诠释，融合民谣、古典、电子与新音乐传统，细节丰富且层次绵密。

items.body:
The classic 12 disc Parmegiani Box Set finally given a reissue by INA GRM, covering the majority of Parmegiani's musique concrète output recorded between 1964 and 2007. Is there a more important, influential, totemic single-artist collection in all of electronic music?

The Wire magazine described it as a "bargain price treasure chest....containing worlds of inexhaustible spaciousness and strangeness" and, indeed, listening through just some of the 12 cd's included you find yourself drawn into a multi-faceted world full of timeless treasure.

Parmegiani was mentored by the founding father of Musique Concrète, Pierre Schaeffer, who made use of technological advances that gave the world magnetic tape and microphones to pioneer a method taking everyday noise and transforming them into unrecognisable sounds, a style that became known as Acousmatic music. 

Parmegiani would go on to make use of these Acousmatic techniques in creating a body of work which is not only one of the most significant of the 20th century, but also hugely influential on a whole host of musical pioneers that would follow in his wake, with Christian Fennesz, Aphex Twin, Kode9 and Jim O'Rourke being notable disciples in the contemporary field. 

It’s hard to comprehend let alone articulate the immersive and often woozy effect of these recordings, ranging from eerie cut-out tape loops through to popular music plunderphonics and proto-distilled-dub that's impossible to absorb in one sitting. In short, L’Œuvre Musicale is one of the most impressive and important collections of electronic music you'll likely ever hear, but also one of the most rewarding.
items._cn_summary: 这张12CD盒装精选收录了Bernard Parmegiani于1964至2007年间创作的具象音乐作品，由法国INA GRM厂牌再版发行。Parmegiani师承Pierre Schaeffer，继承了将日常噪音转化为不可辨识声音的具象音乐技法。其作品涵盖磁带环路、拼贴、声音变形等多种手法，呈现出沉浸式且层次丰富的听觉体验。从诡异的剪切磁带循环到大众音乐解构，再到原始的dub元素，其创作语汇极为丰富。评论强调这套合辑在20世纪电子音乐史中的重要地位，对Christian Fennesz、Aphex Twin、Kode9及Jim O'Rourke等当代音乐人产生了深远影响。该用户口味与具象音乐、电子实验高度契合，INA GRM作为法国实验音乐厂牌亦符合独立厂牌标准。

items.body:
The Necks 18th album Vertigo is an eventful, kaleidoscopic tone poem set against a darkly shimmering background. Slowly but inexorably moving forward, it crosses many frontiers yet remains true to the mission and mood established in the opening stanzas of this cinematic 44 minute journey. A work able to be viewed either as a whole, or two symmetrical halves, Vertigo sees The Necks once again offer an excursion in sound that reflects both the light and darkness of some preternatural world. 

In contrast to the sustained improvisations that are their live performances, The Necks’ studio albums take shape by way of intricate crafting brought to bear throughout the entire recording and mixing process. “The discussion this time really began in earnest in the session itself, where we started to pursue the idea of having a drone running from start to finish, off which we could hang ideas,” said bassist Lloyd Swanton “But like all Necks albums we ended up in a very different place from whatever our initial notion of it had been.” 

Maintaining a teetering tension between suspension and collapse, Vertigo draws on a diverse palette of sounds created in the studio by Tony Buck (drums/percussion/guitar), Lloyd Swanton (bass) and Chris Abrahams (piano/keyboards), featuring everything from homemade instruments, extended instrumental techniques and marathon explorations of sonic textures. 

One piece, at the same time two. Monochrome, yet multicoloured. Dark, yet incandescent. Expansive and still. Melancholic and exhilarating. The Necks. Vertigo."
items._genre: experimental jazz / improvisation / contemporary classical / drone / ambient
items._cn_summary: The Necks 第十八张专辑《Vertigo》以持续嗡鸣的音调（drone）为骨架，在四十四分钟的旅程中缓慢推进，跨越多重音域边界。乐评指出这并非现场即兴录音，而是经过录音与混音全程精心雕琢的产物——贝斯手 Lloyd Swanton 透露三人从录音会话本身出发，逐步构建出一条贯穿始终的低频嗡鸣线，再在其上悬挂各种声音素材，最终却抵达与初始构想截然不同的终点。鼓手 Tony Buck、Swanton 与钢琴家 Chris Abrahams 运用自制乐器、扩展演奏技法及对声学质地的马拉松式探索，编织出在悬浮与崩塌之间维持颤巍巍张力的织体。整张专辑可作为整体聆听，亦可视作两个对称的段落：一元却多彩，幽暗却炽烈，辽阔却静谧，忧郁而振奋。

items.body:
Selected and arranged by Jack Rollo and Elaine Tierney, Ballads’ is a waking-dream meander through beautiful, romantic, weird, exotic, intimate, un-categorisable music that shouldn't go together but yet somehow makes complete sense, offering a sort of spiritual life-enhancement in the process. 

A Colourful Storm’s Fleetway Tapes seems to has become the ideal place for skilled musical storytellers to flex their muscle, and on ‘Ballads’ the London-based duo turn their attention to the classic storytelling category of songcraft with the mix of forensic digging and poetic arrangement that has made their long-running NTS show a cult hit for many. Spanning a literate and cinematic world of sound with signature delicacy, they conjure a far flung and totally absorbing set whose track-listing remains impenetrable, and may well drive diggers to a tizzy. Suffice to say; numerous pearls lie within.

Sung in myriad tongues, the ballads range from the romantic and sentimental to the abstract and instrumental, spieling yarns that may not be fully understood, but with an atmosphere, pacing, and seductive vibe that's unmistakable.

For us, and so many, the mixtape of the decade.
items._genre: mixtape / ballad / experimental curation / world music / poetic arrangement
items._cn_summary: 由Jack Rollo与Elaine Tierney精选编排的这张合辑以'Ballads'为名，却并非传统意义上的情歌集锦，而是一场跨越多种语言、文化与体裁的梦境漫游。两位策展人延续其NTS电台节目一贯的考据精神与诗意编排手法，将看似互不相干的浪漫、异域、抽象与器乐段落编织成一条流畅而隐秘的时间线。专辑曲目以多种语言演唱或纯器乐呈现，氛围与节奏的拿捏取代了语义的可及性，使听者沉入一种既陌生又熟悉的恍惚状态。A Colourystorm旗下的Fleetway Tapes厂牌为这类精细的声音叙事提供了理想庇护所，整张作品如同电影配乐般浩瀚却不张扬，是近年罕见的兼具策展深度与情感密度的混合形态作品。

items.body:
On a ravishing first LP in five years, Arca continues to assume her ultimate form - an HR Giger-esque biomechanical entity; a psychopomp between virtual, physical, and mythological worlds - hallucinating a posthuman club music that feels like the future manifest in her mastery of queer-coded Latin dance and electronic music vernacular.

Leading on from the sprawling ‘Kick’ (2020-21) pentalogy, ‘XXXXX’ consolidates past and present Arca in a sheer vision of club possibilities. Within her 15 year catalogue, the 16-part album appears to balance the ruggedly bittersweet, exploratory spirit of 2013’s ‘&&&&&’ mixtape - a key touchstone of deconstructed dance music - with a more aggressive, yet romantic, thrust that’s emerged thru the ‘Kick’ volumes. Coupled with an ever-finer grasp of the advanced electronica practised by Æ or AFX (or E+E & T C F) which has long underlined her work, and the experience of sharpening her pop talons on Madonna, Rosalía and Kelela records, the results come to light as self-contained album of multitudes, bursting at the seams with fresh yet timeless ideas. 

With the benefit of hindsight it’s not hard to cite Arca as a pied piper of hyper-contemporary electronic music, one instrumental in altering its prevailing rhythmic currency to sexier tresillo permutations, whilst bringing back notions of alien pop in a lineage harking to Bowie via SOPHIE - metaphorically disrupting the status quo and physically changing the way people dance, and both on a really significant scale. ‘XXXXX’ now binds and frays all those strands in her most sharply defined and digestible album statement, eliciting a spectra of emotional responses and proprioceptive sensation with visionary tact and immersive sound design tekkerz.

Geared with a metric, melodic, and spatial freedom that owes to classical music as much as ‘90s electronica and 2010s DAW hyperprisms, the 16 parts unfold from theatric spectralism of ‘No End’, thru the gothic dembow deathknells of ‘Willow’ and fleet hoofed hyperpop of ‘Eidolon’ into singular takes on depth-charged doble paso reggaeton in ’Syncope’, and shearing Ae lines of extended melodic thought on ‘Raver’. A brisk centrepiece ‘Fxck’ is the LP’s horny club anthem in waiting, whilst ‘Finisher’ is maybe the freakier raver’s fave, for its tumultuous dramaturgy of tense strings and displaced braindance-drill trepanation, sharing a deadly torque with the scythe of ‘Grip’ and intense frisson delivered by the saccades of ‘Everything’. Knit with hyperpop prayer ‘Enraptured’, and symphony of harpys summoned on ’Sueño’, it all leaves us in no doubt that Arca is near the apex of her game here.
items._genre: experimental electronic / hyperpop / deconstructed club / queer Latin dance / avant-pop
items._cn_summary: Arca在暌违五年的专辑中完成了形象的最终形态塑造，以生物机械体的姿态横跨虚拟、实体与神话空间。作品延续了《Kick》五部曲的脉络，将早期mixtape的粗粝探索精神与近期更激进而浪漫的推进力熔于一炉，体现出对Æ、AFX一脉前卫电子的精深掌握，以及在与Madonna、Rosalía、Kelela合作中打磨出的流行敏感度。十六首曲目在古典音乐自由度的结构中展开，从歌剧幽灵般的谱系出发，穿过哥特dembow、疾蹄hyperpop、深度律动doble paso reggaeton，直至神经外科般的braindance-drill碎片。整张专辑呈现出锐利而可消化的面貌，声音设计沉浸而富有远见，将异族流行传统、拉丁舞曲语汇与俱乐部未来主义编织成一体。

items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.
items.label: Songs of Compassion
items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 联合前卫作曲家 Paladino 与诗人 Ferrari，推出专辑《Songs of Compassion》。十一首作品以钢琴为核心，辅以弦乐、木管与合成器织体，运用微分音与去调性手法打破西方和声惯例，旋律如意识流般延展。Moskowitz 的演唱沉稳老练，将每个词的语义置于旋律之上，钢琴如同希腊合唱队般参与叙事。歌词直面当下议题，《Pale Wanderer》揭示极权主义的共谋机制，《Charlottesville》追忆火炬游行事件中的种族主义话语，整体延续六十年代抗议诗传统，兼具哲思与时政批判。音乐不提供抚慰，而是以解构方式邀请听众重新审视被束缚的听觉经验。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: The Breedling的专辑《A Straunge And Terrible Wunder》以英国东盎格利亚传说中的地狱犬Black Shuck为灵感，纪念其神秘显灵的第449周年。制作人Chris Spalton运用无人机音、合成器与田野录音等手段，构建出一张以黑暗色调为主的氛围作品，将英国最古老的超自然民俗现象引入当代语境。整张专辑被描述为从深处被拖拽上来的声响，呈现出不安与压迫感，融合了工业声响的研磨质感与氛围音乐的幽暗层次。The Quietus的乐评将这张专辑定位为有意令人不安的声音实验，借助历史与神话的题材框架，展开对声音黑暗面的探索。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Aether, created in 2021 by four friends, initially began as a project for bassist Andrea's final thesis, with the aim of moving away from conventional jazzy sounds. Their sound blends post-rock, contemporary classical rock, and multi-layered jazzy prog."Oort Cloud" is a prime example, fusing ambient, jazzy tones, and dino-tinged progressive rock reminiscent of King Crimson, with a flute buzzing here and there. A long, contemplative suite encourages a dreamlike journey, with a primal Fender Rhodes piano accompanying the oppressive psychedelic guitar riff. "Vogon" opens with Collins' electronic drums, then shifts to a jazzier feel with Claudio Milano's frenetic narration. The air soars on Zappa-esque jazz-rock guitar in the purest tradition, flirting with the great Return To Forever on the distinctive piano; a frenetic finale with infectious energy. "Five Shades, Four Frames" opens with a spacey sound, a prominent rhythmic bassline. A drift into hyperspace follows this encroaching Crimson-esque crescendo; improvisation steers clear of interstellar notes. Midway through, the sound takes on an Arabic quality, reminiscent of a Star Wars desert, over a psychedelic Tangerine Dream melody. The obvious jazzy Rhodes turn on a drumbeat with a hint of Steven Wilson is surprising."The Melancholy of the Little Prince" features a melancholic piano drifting over percussion and electronic notes, giving free rein to the fretless bass. Musical scales, a crackling, distorted sound as if from a parallel universe. "Panta Rei" sees the flute searching for its footing, wandering notes for a learned musical digression; jazz, unmistakably King Crimson, Andrea's guitar surfing avant-garde territory for a controlled jumble. Dynamic and apocalyptic with its explosive contemporary finale, "Swerve" opens with a snowy, religious, ethereal feel. The captivating keyboards lead into post-rock territory illuminated by scores reminiscent of Porcupine Tree. The track then veers into jazzy soft rock territory with a distinctive piano demon unleashing a fury, recounting the new Italian sound.Aether brilliantly dares to create a jazzy post-rock fusion, injecting a dose of ambient and modern prog, opening this movement to the contemporary world.
items._genre: post-rock / math rock / jazz fusion / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: Aether 由四位意大利乐手于 2021 年组建，最初是贝斯手 Andrea 的毕业项目，意在脱离传统爵士框架。专辑以长篇套曲为核心手法，将后摇、当代古典摇滚与多层爵士前奏编织在一起。《Oort Cloud》以 Fender Rhodes 电钢琴铺设梦境，压迫感迷幻吉他 riff 与长笛点缀交织；《Vogon》在 Collins 电子鼓点与米兰诺叙事之间切换，键盘线条向 Return to Forever 致敬；《Five Shades, Four Frames》展现太空感贝斯线后转入阿拉伯音阶段落，类似 Tangerine Dream 的合成器旋律浮现沙漠意象；《The Melancholy of the Little Prince》以无品贝斯即兴释放情绪，平行宇宙般的失真声响穿插其中；《Panta Rei》让长笛与吉他在 King Crimson 式混沌中对话；《Swerve》则以宗教氛围开头，键盘领入 Porcupine Tree 风格的后摇段落。整体以爵士后摇融合为核心，大胆开辟新意大利声响的可能性。

items.body: Redemption the salvation That’s out of reach All the lies they will forever preach The night belongs to vampires, black leather, bad blood, and decisions best made after the sun has gone down. The Lost Boys sank its fangs into theatres on the 31 of July 1987, and Karlsruhe industrial death wave trio Bleak Monday chose the same date 39 years later to unleash Shelter. It feels like an appropriately cursed bit of calendar alignment. The song and its accompanying video share the film’s appetite for danger, nocturnal excess, temptation, and the enduring truth that everyone looks better once respectable society has locked its doors and drawn the curtains. Bleak Monday takes that invitation underground, descending into a dungeon club where the congregation wears black, the entertainment comes with cages, and somebody has clearly misplaced both the fire code and the holy water. Bleak Monday formed in Karlsruhe in December 2022 with one foot in ’80s wave and the other planted somewhere between metal, industrial rock, and the more bruising end of electronic music. Skinny Puppy, Nine Inch Nails, and Ministry provide useful coordinates, though there is also enough dangerous glamour here to imagine the song turning up midway through a particularly depraved Gregg Araki sequence. Directed by Natascha Gaballo, the video drops Bleak Monday into a dungeon club populated by cages, goth go-go dancers, temptation, domination, and enough black vinyl to make a parish priest reconsider his evening plans. The footage was transferred to VHS and then re-digitized, giving the images the bruised texture of an ’80s B-movie that spent several years behind the counter at a video store before somebody finally asked what was on it. Horror references tied to singer Kim Ryder’s favorite films are tucked into the scenery for anyone inclined to freeze-frame their way through the debauchery. That presentation suits Shelter, a slab of industrial death wave built from Yann Lauer’s guitar, Sebastian “Hubu” Huber’s synths, drums, and bass, and Ryder’s commanding vocal performance. Ryder sings about religious hypocrisy, concealed abuse, televised violence, and salvation sold by institutions that appear to have misplaced the receipt. The central plea for rescue grows increasingly desperate as the song works through shame, faith, exploitation, and spiritual exhaustion. Any promise of redemption feels compromised by the people making it, leaving the singer caught between belief, disgust, and the desire to disappear from a reality that has become unbearable. Gaballo makes that unease physical. Ryder performs amid bodies presented as spectacle, pleasure, threat, and distraction, while the club becomes both sanctuary and trap. The cages are hardly subtle, but subtlety would be rather pointless when the song is throwing death, rape, hypocrisy, and redemption into the room. Sometimes a sledgehammer has admirable editorial instincts. Watch the video for Shelter below: Shelter also serves as a teaser for Bleak Monday’s forthcoming debut album, Bad Music, a title that practically invites hostile witnesses. Since beginning live shows in early 2023, the trio have shared stages with Das Kinn, Nils Keppel, The Body, and Ministry. Judging from this clip, they have already figured out one valuable lesson: if civilization is collapsing, somebody should at least book the dancers. Listen to Shelter below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评介绍德国卡尔斯鲁厄三人组Bleak Monday的单曲《Shelter》及其MV。乐队成立于2022年底，音乐风格融合八十年代暗潮、死亡浪潮、工业摇滚与电子乐的粗粝面向，参考坐标包括Skinny Puppy、九寸钉与Ministry。歌曲以工业死亡浪潮的质感构建，吉他、合成器、鼓与贝斯交织，配以极具控制力的女声vocal，主题围绕宗教虚伪、被掩盖的虐待、电视暴力以及制度兜售的救赎展开，中心诉求随歌曲推进而愈发绝望。MV由Natascha Gaballo执导，画面转入地下俱乐部场景，哥特舞者、笼子、支配与诱惑交织，并将素材转制为VHS再数字化，营造出八十年代B级片的磨损质感。整体呈现出对夜间、危险、诱惑与宗教伪善的视觉与听觉双重隐喻。

items.body:
Peak Oil sublabel FO returns with a strong debut of late night, air-fried trip hop from Cold Light, flocking like moths to an illbient flame tipped FFO Jabu, Tricky, Sleepdial, Shell Company, Space Afrika.

Cold Light are Bristol’s Birthmark & Withdrawn, Portland’s Best Available Technology, Rael & Eldon out of London, and Hungarian CSNL. Some half a decade after a ‘Live at the Laundromat’ tape introduction, the collective unveil ‘Coldtron 2’, a sparingly sensuous slant on the lush pastures between trip hop, smoked-out dub soul and illbient jazz, inflected with the voices of Elaine Malone, Akeko and British-Nigerian sound designer Tony Onuchukwu. With remarkable restraint - especially considering so many hands are on board - they keep everything pared-back to creaking, atmospheric fundamentals for 40 minutes of smouldering storytelling, passing the torch across chapters of zoot-end poetic monologues, from stylised rap to spoken word, in a spectrum of accents speaking to the group’s far flung coordinates. 

Call it downbeat neo-noir or trip hop 2.0, the sound is clearly in thrall to the ‘90s OGs - Tricky, Portishead, Massive Attack - yet gauzily distinguished from its forebears by the production’s pall of dematerialised textures and an enervated feel for screwed subs and glimmers of sounds that emerged in trip hop’s fall-out. The Bristol night air is thick with sferic crackle and diffused sax in ’Smoke Signal’ thru the Memotone-esque eldritch of ‘Troposphere Test’, taking in a tacit nod to Mobb Deep via Tricky on the smouldering ‘Riot’, or even Civilistjävel!’s low-key electrodub in ‘Lean Wid It…’,    and Sleepdial’s slurred drums on ‘I’ve Known Fires’. But they’re most potent on ‘Fields in B’ with eight mins of smudged Rhythm & Sound steppas bass anchoring the bluest sax plumes and blunted bars, ideal for ashtray dreamers.
items._genre: trip hop / illbient / dub / electronic / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由分散于布里斯托尔、波特兰、伦敦和匈牙利的音乐人组成的集体创作的夜间氛围专辑，将trip hop、烟雾感的dub灵魂乐与illbient爵士融合在一起。制作保持了显著的克制力，将声响削至最低限度的环境骨架，用嘶嘶的无线电干扰、弥散的萨克斯和拧紧的低频构建叙事氛围。专辑跨越诗歌独白、说唱与口语表演等多种人声形式，形成多章节式的叙事结构。在致敬Tricky、Portishead、Massive Attack等九零年代经典的同时，融入了screwed subs、ambient dematerialised textures等后trip hop的实验元素，八分钟的Fields in B以Rhythm & Sound式的steppers低音和蓝色萨克斯呈现出最具沉浸感的段落。

items.body:
jason calhoun’s fifth release for Dear Life Records,

"On revelations of divine love Calhoun has assembled an especially potent album of work that whirrs, hums, and glows. Unlike his recent output centered around extended, hypnotic compositions, the fourteen tracks here immediately request your attention and curiosity. Their concision only underscores one of his greatest strengths: the ability to capture an evaporating, fleeting moment, and hold it close.

The title is a nod to British Anchoress Julian of Norwich, whose collected writing of the same title is the earliest of any woman written in English. Here it serves as a unifying theme for Calhoun's particular palette of restless textures and tentative melodies. This is personal music, to be sure, but it also feels tactile, almost taffy-like in its presentation—and with such a potent combination, it is hard to resist a smile while listening. Like when the insistent pulse grounding 'last one' suddenly changes color as yawning tones reveal themselves, or how 'eye dilation' tiptoes into the room with each note sounding like a carefully chosen step. Though never precious or fussy, the album remains resolutely intimate.

Calhoun puts it plainly: “Julian of Norwich says “‘All shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well’. These days, I’ve been having my doubts that this is true. As no solution to the issue at hand, I look for the revelations of divine love in my life, and I find them--in my partner asleep on the floor in our studio, my survival of a social interaction with a stranger, being bad at chess. Don't ask me what they mean-I'm still figuring that out myself. Maybe we can figure it out together.” It is from this place of doubt, searching, and openness that the album finds its footing."
items._cn_summary: Jason Calhoun 在 Dear Life Records 发行的第五张专辑收录了十四首短小精炼的作品，标题源自英国隐修者朱利安·诺里奇的同名著作，作为统一主题串联起不安分的声响肌理与试探性的旋律线条。评论指出这些曲目与 Calhoun 此前的长篇催眠式作曲形成对比，以紧凑的结构迅速攫取听者注意力，展现了他捕捉稍纵即逝瞬间并将其凝固的能力。制作上呈现出粘稠、近乎可触摸的质感，脉搏般的节奏与逐渐显露的音调色彩在特定曲目中交替出现，整体保持亲密的内省气质。Calhoun 本人引用朱利安的"一切都将安然无恙"作为引子，坦承当下对此的怀疑，转而在日常生活碎片——熟睡的伴侣、一场社交互动的完成、一局糟糕的象棋——中寻找神性启示的踪迹。整张专辑立足于怀疑、探寻与开放的状态，邀请听者共同参与意义的建构。

items.body:
The Mitteleuropa enigma is strong on the 2nd original LP by Pablo’s Eye for Stroom, commanding attention to noctilucent, cinematic synth scapes laced with hand-played drums and poetry that plays out like a waking dream.

Active since ’89, the rotating assembly of Pablo’s Eye, headed by Axel Libeert, have plotted a unique course thru the backwaters of art rock, ambient, fantasy soundtrack music, and whatever else they fancy, leading to a pair of retrospectives on Stroom in 2018-19, plus the cult EP ‘Bardo For Pablo’, and fresh material on ‘The Light Was Sharp, Our Eyes Were Closed’ (2024).

Here represented by Marie Mandi, Luc Laret, Thierry Royo, Richard Skinner, Axel Libeert, and Ludwig Lapauw on ‘Everything You Give Away’, they follow noses for a typically low slung and resoundingly atmospheric album primed to seduce anyone in its path, as they stealthily proceed from the nightfall of ‘Walking the Line’, reminding us of DAAC, to the blushed choral pads and trip hop bass of ‘Reverie’ and Reese bass-gilded centrepiece ‘A dash of raspberry’, and ultimately the widescreen departure of ‘October ’75’. 

Trés classy.

items._cn_summary: 比利时（透过中欧视角）音乐人 Axel Libeert 主导的 Pablo's Eye 计划推出第二张正式专辑，延续其自1989年以来的折衷路线。作品融合电影化的合成器音景与手打鼓机，营造出夜光般的冥想氛围，并嵌入诗歌念白，构筑如同清醒之梦般的叙事。专辑从黄昏般的开场曲过渡到带合唱垫音与trip-hop低音的曲目，再到以Reese低音为装饰的核心段落，最终以宽银幕式的史诗感收尾。整体呈现出低调但层次丰富的氛围美学，介于幻想电影配乐、art rock与ambient之间，对偏好实验性氛围与跨界融合的听众具有较强吸引力。

items.body:
Seoul’s Uman Thurman & Yetsuby, aka Salamanda, meditate on the inner life of a basil plant with a delicately flavoured suite of pottering pulses and harmonised warmth in a fine tradition of Far Eastern ambient electronica that chimes with label mates at GMT and the likes of E Ruscha V or Woo.

“The album moves through a full day in the plant's life opening with ‘introduce my atom which is my favorite one’, an act of quiet self-declaration in morning light, before settling into the unhurried rhythmic pulse of ‘to to ki toki tok’- the drip of water, the tick of a clock, the slow beat of photosynthesis. ‘allez, pousse!’ - one of the standouts in this journey - carries the basil's gentle will to grow, to push, to tilt toward the sun, while ‘hungry snail’ captures a moment of creaturely encounter on the glass: an uninvited visitor, moving slowly, wanting. As the afternoon deepens, 'Basil's Ritual' traces the daily ceremony of light and warmth, repeated with calm devotion from root to leaf. Night falls across 'Basil's Dream', and in the stillness something like sleep arrives - the plant resting, imagining tomorrow's sun. The album closes with ‘the blue wine’, a final mysterious reverie in which the basil seems to contemplate its own fate, somewhere between acceptance and wonder.”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以一株罗勒植物的昼夜生长为隐喻，将整个生命周期编织为八首曲目，从清晨的自我宣告到午后的光合节拍，从玻璃上的蜗牛偶遇到夜晚的梦境沉思。音乐以细腻的脉冲节奏与和声温度为核心，呈现东方气质的氛围电子风格，与GMT厂牌、E Ruscha V或Woo等人的脉络相呼应。作品不以炫技或繁复层次取胜，而是以缓慢、呼吸般的节奏感营造冥想氛围，音景设计倾向于有机质感——水滴声、时钟滴答、光线变化都被转化为听觉事件。整体呈现出一种安静的园艺式冥想气质，适合在专注或放松状态下聆听，乐评对每首曲目的叙事定位清晰，但音乐本身的实验深度仍有进一步探索的空间。

items.body:
Anyone smote by DINTE’s ‘Begena Songs…’ will be properly enchanted by this more expansive - yet still intimate - suite of snapshots from Ethiopia, ’71, spanning the unique, twanging harp sound thru to Amharic poetry, Afar chants, and spellbinding flutes dances

One that catches the breath with seldom felt sensations, ‘Ethiopian Musics 1971’ patently owes as much to the incredible performers as their faithful representation in Ragnar Johnson & Ralph Harrisson’s recordings. All secreted to tape on a Uher Report L stereo reel-to-reel recorder, they epitomise an era of ethnomusicological preservation, when the likes of labels such as Lyrichord and  Folkways were already decades deep “in the field”, documenting long-held traditions practically untouched by an encroaching, western modernity. And perhaps most crucially, the recordings beautifully render the acoustic settings and vivid vibes with an immersive quality in stark opposition to the era of dry, so-called audiophile studio recordings of ethnic musics to come - all the better for immersing in this wonderfully unfamiliar world.

The abundance of singular tones and strong, rare feels they produce is quite staggering to our northern english ears, and we reckon also for anyone else, for that matter. Opening to a joyful couplet of a bluesy ’Song about the beauty of women’, and the almost shanty-like swing and hard rhythm of ’Tej Beit Song’, the set reels to distinctive pieces of Ethiopian Christian song set to begena, or ‘Harp of David’, buzz, and a landscape-scale, 13 minute ‘Love Song (Mary Armede)’. A gripping ‘Drum Song (Jigsaw)’ will be mana to rhythm fiends, and a number of standout flute pieces reprise the frisson of our first encounter with this discipline on Sublime Freq’s ‘Staring into the Sun - Ethiopian Tribal Music’ set of 2012, most potently on the pluming twin pipes of the ‘Fila Flute Dance’ parts, whilst the pentatonic craar (6-stringed lyre) parts surely strike nerves for lovers of the rawest blues, and hail the liberated legacy of Mary Armede, a folk singer-fashion designer of Azmari heritage who surely warrants further investigation. 

No doubt this is one of the most striking archival discoveries of 2026, acutely advised to anyone enchanted with music from this corner of the world from Éthiopiques to begena harp, thru to Ragnar Johnson’s other arenas of research for Ideologic Organ in Yemen or Papua New Guinea. Dive in without delay.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张于1971年由Ragnar Johnson与Ralph Harrisson在埃塞俄比亚实地录制的民族音乐档案，呈现了独特的拨弦竖琴begena、六弦琴craar、竹笛及Azmari诗歌等多种传统音乐形式。录音使用Uher Report L立体声便携式开盘机完成，保留了原声场地的空间感与鲜活氛围，与后来干燥的录音棚民族音乐制作形成鲜明对比。专辑收录了女性民间歌手兼时装设计师Mary Armede的13分钟情歌，以及令人屏息的Fila Flute Dance双管笛曲。作为民族音乐学保存工作的代表，此作延续了Lyrichord与Folkways等厂牌的田野录音传统，展现了西部现代性尚未触及的非洲音乐原貌。

items.body:
'Passiflora' is the tenth edition of Music To Watch Seeds Grow By, and the fourth of Season Two. Work conceived, collected and collaged by KiF Productions. ​

"Passiflora (Passifloraceae) is a genus of around 550 species of flowering plants, native to the tropical and subtropical Americas. The Passion Flower is a plant of improbable beauty - its blooms almost too intricate to be real, its climbing habit a quiet kind of determination. It has been used for centuries as a remedy for anxiety and sleeplessness, something that slows us and the world around us down.

Fresh from last year's triumphant debut by KiF; Still Out, Passiflora, the album, follows the plant from its very beginning. It opens in darkness - 'Secret of the Seed', dormant, waiting - before the first tentative stir of 'First Movement' and the long, instinctive reach of 'Seeking Light'. From there, the journey unfolds with the patience of something that has no choice but to grow: drinking, climbing, flowering. 'Song of the Vine' carries the plant's quiet insistence upward, while 'Florescence' and 'Pollination Dream' catch it at its most open - that brief, extraordinary moment of full bloom. Then the turn. 'Fruiting (Slight Return)' and finally 'Return to Earth' - the cycle completing itself, giving back what it always borrowed.

Each track is a stage. The whole is a life cycle."
items._cn_summary: 《Passiflora》是Music To Watch Seeds Grow By系列的第十期作品，以西番莲花为隐喻构建了一部完整的生命循环声乐作品。KiF Productions采用拼贴手法，将声音编织成一株植物从黑暗中的种子状态出发，经历萌发、攀爬、开花、结果的完整生命周期。曲目命名遵循植物学逻辑——'Secret of the Seed'起于沉睡与等待，'Song of the Vine'承载向上攀爬的力量，'Florescence'与'Pollination Dream'捕捉盛放时刻的短暂壮丽，最终以'Return to Earth'归还所借之物。整体编排以极简材料模拟生长节律，弱化旋律走向，转向质地与时间的展开。文本将声音与生物学叙事并置，赋予专辑近似概念艺术的框架，适合在低光环境下长时间聆听。

items.body:
Ambient composer Natalia Beylis leads an ensemble of Nyahh’s finest in her landscape-shaped evocation of a field in Leitrim, Éire, quietly meditating on the natural logic of birds and trees.

‘Around Here The Birds Plant The Trees’ is Beylis’ slow-burn, long-form arrangement for quintet - Eimear Reidy (cello), Tola Custy (fiddle), Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh & Ultan O’Brien (violin), and Willie Stewart (percussion) - seeded in her reading of a blackbird’s dawn chorus, and subsequent conversation with a local farmer on how “birds are the architects of the living landscape”. It follows some 40 solo albums over the past 20 years (not to mention jams with Woven Skull and Tomuttontu) with a considered approach to what lies just beyond her home; typically drawing on her attentive reading of the rural soundsphere to transmute the poetry of birdsong and the natural world into expressive musical metaphor.

The low bowed cello tone of regular spar Eimear Reidy underlines and opens out a breezy space where where the fiddle and violinists criss-cross air in reserved melodic flight and plucky figures that alternate like the play of light on Ireland’s remote North West. The piece unfolds to boggy pockets of percussion and passages of barely-there, hushed gloam, as though the wind itself was generating the players’ gestures, which rise to cloud castle hover around the midway, only to depart for Nyahh label boss Willie Stewart’s rolling drum thunder and scrape of Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh's fiddle rooted in the rolling landscape. Ultimately the folk soul of the turf rises in its final section, resembling a rousing, swaying folk song voiced by the strings in ideally creaky discord.

items._cn_summary: 爱尔兰环境音乐作曲家娜塔莉亚·贝利斯以利特里姆郡的田野为灵感，创作了一首为五重奏而作的慢速展开长篇作品。作品缘起于她聆听黑鸫破晓鸣唱后与当地农人的对话，从中提炼出'鸟类是活态景观的建筑师'这一意象。大提琴低沉弓奏奠定基调，小提琴与提琴在空旷空间中交织出克制的旋律线条，呼应爱尔兰西北部光影的变幻。作品逐步推进至沼泽般的打击乐段落与近乎无声的幽微时刻，中段旋律如云堡般悬浮，下半段由鼓声与提琴摩擦构成翻滚的戏剧张力，最终在弦乐苍茫的和声中收束，呈现出土地之上的民谣灵魂。整张专辑以自然声响为隐喻，将鸟类歌唱的诗意转译为器乐语言，融合当代作曲手法与爱尔兰传统音乐质感。

items.body:
Cloud-seeding dub techno sorcery x Rhythm & Sound worship by Stephen Hitchell’s cult cv313 and Radius projects, recorded in the heart of Detroit and preserved for posterity by Pole’s faithful remasters at Scape Berlin.

Echospace co-pilot Stephen Hitchell mans the cockpit solo on six sterling examples of Motor City dub techno purism within the 1st volume of ‘Altering Illusions’. His hallucinatory, synaesthetic tekkerz are in palpable effect from the damp bass thru to its noctilucent synth haze, bathing bodies in blissed-out arrangements that unfold up to 20 minutes in length, as with the echoes of BC’s ‘radiance’ registered in expansive parting piece ‘standing still’, and dredged up from drizzly depths on the cv313 rewire of Radius’ ‘Interpolation Tapes’.

Clubs are in the rearview for an 80 min trip deep under the hood of Echospace’s classic sound, fathoming deepest levels of sunken subs and elemental attrition on ‘i s i s’, and hingeing on Rhythm & Sound’s skankers' templates in ‘hypnosphere’ and mesmerising metallic resonance of ‘irradiate’, while ‘above clouds’ rises above the weather system into clearer, blue-skied dub techno lushness; think post-storm Lake Erie panoramas diffused by Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Stephen Hitchell以cv313名义在底特律录制的dub techno作品，由柏林厂牌Scape发行，Pole担任母带处理。共收录六首作品，时长约八十分钟，多首曲目接近二十分钟，呈现深沉的低频和朦胧的合成器氛围。制作上汲取了Rhythm & Sound的skank节奏模板，同时融入GAS式的环境音景质感，作品之间在dub回响、sub-bass和金属共鸣之间游走。从潮湿的贝斯线条到夜光般的合成器雾气，整体走向偏向俱乐部之外的聆听体验，强调空间感和延展性。评论将其定位为Echospace经典声音的深度呈现，适合偏好ambient质感与dub回响结构的听众。

items.body:
Somewhere between more eaze, Susan Alcorn and Daniel Lanois, 'Langliek', the first album from pedal-steel masters Geir Sundstøl and Joe Harvey-Whyte, is a taste of bliss, a hazy, horizontal duet on guitar, organ, Moog and drum machine.

It's hard not to immediately warm to this one. The pedal-steel's an underused instrument, to be honest, and one that suits "ambient" music remarkably well, we've known this at least since Lanois introduced it to Brian Eno's arsenal of sounds on the milestone 'Apollo: Atmospheres and Soundtracks'. And even though Norwegian multi-instrumentalist Sundstøl and London-based player Harvey-Whyte have been refining their craft individually for years, the latter playing with everyone from Josephine Foster to Billy Bragg and the former contributing to literally hundreds of albums, it's that record that still serves as the creative anchor for their collaboration.

The duo began chatting in 2016 when Harvey-Whyte discovered Sundstøl's solo album 'Furulund', and they continued chatting and visiting each others' studios until 2024 when Harvey-Whyte took a break from touring to spend a week in Oslo. They worked spontaneously, which was a surprise for Sundstøl, who usually spends months tweaking each little detail, and relied on their improvisations on pedal-steel to set the pace of each piece. Adding elements from Sundstøl's arsenal of instruments (including an Optigan, a rare optical keyboard, and a set of Moog synths, the duo turned their improvisations into a full album, conjuring up a mood that genuinely felt Norwegian.

Of course, it's hard to separate the instrument from its American roots, but the duo pull out the edges of Americana just far enough to justify the album's title, a reference to a Norwegian folk instrument. You can just about hear the snow crunching in the background and see a hint of neon green in the sky, if you look carefully.

items._cn_summary: 两位踏板钢吉他演奏家首次合作的专辑，将美国根源乐器与北欧氛围美学融合。专辑在吉他、风琴、Moog合成器和鼓机之间构建了一种慵懒的横向对话，借鉴了Lanois为Eno《Apollo》引入踏板钢吉他时所建立的氛围传统。两位音乐人各自拥有丰富的合作履历，从2016年开始通过互访工作室逐渐发展出共同语言，最终在2024年用一周时间在奥斯陆即兴录制完成。制作中使用了罕见的Optigan光学键盘和Moog合成器，将踏板钢吉他的即兴线条延伸为完整的氛围作品。专辑标题指向挪威传统乐器Langeleik，音乐气质也呼应了挪威的地理氛围——雪地、北极光式的霓虹色调，以及被拉远到几乎抽象的美式根源音乐质感。这是一种介于乡村、氛围和电子实验之间的跨界实践。

items.body:
Cathedral is a thrilling album and terrifying graphic novel from director and musician John Carpenter, based on a dream Carpenter had in 2024.

"An abandoned cathedral. A gruesome murder. A powerful supernatural entity living in the catacombs. It all comes to a head in downtown Los Angeles. What will happen and who will live to tell the tale? Such is the storyline of Cathedral, it has all the drama, dark atmosphere, and frenetic pacing of a classic heavy metal record. Especially designed as the soundtrack to the graphic novel, each track corresponds to a specific section of the book. The liner notes included with the album packaging feature prompts for each track, creating a fully interactive experience. Combined with the graphic novel, it’s the closest thing to a new John Carpenter film in years.

The music on Cathedral retains all the eerie atmosphere and sinister propulsion of the epochal scores Carpenter created for his films Halloween, The Fog, and Assault on Precinct 13, but this is a much heavier, riff-driven enterprise. Carpenter is a firm believer that music plays a major role in what really makes something scary. That’s first and foremost,” the director says. “It’s all about making the music work.” “This is somewhat different sounding stuff that we’ve done, but it’s done with the same desire in mind,” he adds. “In other words, put this thing on and imagine you’re watching a movie. That’s what we want you to do.”

Daniel Davies’ soaring, snaky guitars take center stage on opener “Primeval,” “Elevator,” and the metal masterpiece “Lord of the Underground” while John Carpenter and Cody Carpenter’s synths take the lead on the ominous “Desolation in the Underworld,” the plaintive “Death of the Mapmaker,” and even converge with strings on “Abandoned Cathedral.”

Whereas the Lost Themes albums were written as scores to movies of the mind, Cathedral scores the first original graphic novel written by Carpenter, his wife and long-time creative partner, producer and editor Sandy King, and writer Sean Sobczak, published by Storm King Comics."

items._cn_summary: 《Cathedral》是约翰·卡彭特与儿子及音乐伙伴戴维斯合作的概念专辑，配合同名图像小说发行，灵感源于导演2024年的一个梦境。专辑呈现出废弃教堂、地下墓穴中的超自然实体等叙事场景，融合了卡彭特标志性的合成器恐怖氛围与重金属的强劲节奏驱动。戴维斯的吉他蜿蜒穿梭于多首曲目中，而卡彭特父子的合成器则主导了阴郁与哀婉的段落，三件乐器在终曲中汇合。专辑不仅是音乐，也是图像小说的配套声轨，每首曲目对应漫画特定章节，歌词册中嵌入阅读提示，形成沉浸式跨界体验。相比此前的《Lost Themes》系列，这部作品更加厚重、更加偏向金属化处理，将七十年代恐怖电影的阴冷配器转化为当代重型的器乐表达。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Minos is one of Quebec's best example of electronic prog with Dionne-Bregent's 2� Jour andPritchard's Earthworm Stew. Languirand's followed the trend of other synth wizards by playing all ofthe intruments himself and bothers to sing (+/- acceptably so) , but what comes out of the ordinaryis Pascal's use of the Moog Taurus, giving an amazingly deep bass tone. Languirand had majored in cinematography from Concordia University and a lot of his tracks were accompanied with small films.Opening on the cosmic Alpha 700, we already know we're about travel into the upper layers of thesky, and the Taurus bass pedals are used in a very singular manner, ricocheted by his searingguiter. You'll find the same kind of climate in Oiseau de Crystal and Megalopolis. Orient has acelestial mood gruising over India's troposphere, which is so�ewhat of a departure, but it won't bethe only one.On the flipside, we have a weird atypical folky tun that doesn't fit with the rest of the album, the7-mins Dans Le Vent, where Pascal gives voice orally. The closing 12-mins Omega is a minor tour deforce, making you think of Crazy Diamond's unearthing, but shaped by Schulze or Froese. Somewhere stuck between Heldon and Schulze with a pinch of Floyd, Minos has its own distinctiveflavour and is well worth the detour to look for it (none of his album have been reissued in CD,however).
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1978年来自魁北克的电子前卫专辑。演奏者Languirand包揽全部乐器并兼任人声，毕业于康考迪亚大学电影学专业，部分作品搭配自制短片发行。整张专辑的核心特色在于对Moog Taurus低音踏板的独特运用——这种处理方式产生出异常深沉的低音音色，与他尖锐的吉他形成反弹式呼应。开场曲Alpha 700营造出宇宙感氛围，Oiseau de Crystal与Megalopolis延续这一基调，Orient转向印度对流层的异国色调。B面收录一段7分钟非典型民谣小品Dans Le Vent，与专辑整体走向形成断裂；压轴曲Omega长达12分钟，展现出Schulze与Froese式的结构展开。整体定位介于Heldon与Schulze之间，融入Pink Floyd的幽冥色彩，尚未发行CD版本。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — Fruupp, for years lived under the shadows of giants, as an opening act for bands like Genesis orKing Crimson, working hard to get recognition, the quintet was prolific in every sense of the word,and despite never getting any commercial success, some of their influence can be felt on genres suchas math rock or symphonic prog.Before the actual review starts, I'd like to take a moment to do something I am not acostumed to inthis site, I'd like to give the band some extra points for their wonderful sleeve art, which is aninteresting mix of medieval, impressionist and dadaist styles...unlike many eclectic covers whichare absurd for the sake of absurdity itself, this cover is absurd but also hides intention andartistic quality, anyone dedicated enough to aesthetics will get what I mean. It's a beautifulsleeve indeed.Starting off with that which is the absolute strength of this record : It's creativity and uniqueapproach. Northern Ireland had been a colony under British imperial rule for quite a while at thatpoint, so it's natural that aspects of cultural syncretism are to be felt across the 39 minutes ofmusic this album has, yet, it keeps most of the Irish musical identity intact, this is an act ofcultural resistance, but mixed with a proper dose of syncretism, it feels innovative, if they hadgone a little more British, then it would have hit the uncanny valley, yet this is not the case. Iwas quite surprised to learn that this band is not Iberian either, since strangely enough some ofthe modes, scales and rhythmic patterns are borrowed from Iberian music, this adds to a refreshingMediterranean sound mixed with strong Celtic influence, it's quite funny how well these two stylesfit together in the record, since it *shouldn't* be that way as their almost opposite philosophiesin the way they approach this art. I also noticed some faint Arabic influences, but they are smalland barely noticeable, it's on tracks such as "Graveyard Epistle" where it can truly be felt...butit might as well just be the Iberian influence I mentioned before, since iberia is stronglyinfluenced by the Arab world due go the 700 years it spent under Arabic rule.The quality of the compositions is rich and diverse, despite being relatively short (between the 4and 8 minutes mark), they have several small movements, leitmotifs and variations, it's rhythmicallydense and that's it's clearest identity factor, across the record, the intricate and delicatepercussions, bass lines and guitars are condensed in a dance and struggle against each other,pushing to their limits and then coming together in complex polyrhythms, metrics and lines thatsyncopate and then go into chaos, over and over, it's hypnotic! The track "Song for a thought" is agreat example of this, it also incorporates classic Rock and roll elements. Then comes theambient textures, oboes, string ensembles, delayed and reversed guitars and some clicking cymbals createan ambience of immersion and psychedelia which is ethereal in nature, it induces a high state ofconcentration and doesn't contradict the complex rhythms, if anything it complements them.If I had to describe the sound of this record in a single sentence it'd be : Baroque andmulticultural, vanguardist yet hypnotic...feels fresh even in 2026, which is 50+ years since it'srelease.The musicianship is great, and there's a natural chemistry between them all that holds thecompositions together like a glue, they are technically prominent (although not gifted) and have agreat sense of melody and rhythm, their teamwork is astonishing, specially the lead singers voicewhich is similar to Lake from ELP and Shulman from gentle giant. The production is okay, it doesfeel rough and noisy at times but putting this into context (underground act mainly known by collegestudents in Britain) it's understandable, it's something you can overlook if you will, andprobably will do so anyways because of how hypnotic this all is.Fans of gentle giant will love this since it feels a lot like "Acquiring the taste" (specially theslower, violin driven parts), the similarities are astounding, the band had not yet reached theirfull identity yet, but it's enjoyable anyways.A solid 5/5!

items._cn_summary: 这张1973年专辑来自北爱尔兰五人乐队，是一部融合凯尔特音乐身份与伊比利亚、阿拉伯等地中海元素的跨文化作品，在英国殖民的文化背景下呈现出抵抗与融合的张力。专辑每首曲目虽控制在4至8分钟，却通过多重乐段、主导动机与变奏构建出节奏密集的复调织体，吉他、贝斯与打击乐在复杂的多节拍与切分中相互角力又彼此呼应，形成催眠式的循环律动。配器上采用双簧管、弦乐合奏、延迟与倒置吉他以及清脆的钹声，营造沉浸式的氛围纹理。封面艺术融合中世纪、印象派与达达主义风格，兼具荒诞感与艺术意图。整体展现了非主流地区乐队在交响前卫摇滚框架中融入多元文化声音的独特探索。

items.body: A pair of heavy hitting body music tours set to make their way across North America this fall ended up booking shows in Vancouver on the same day, and thankfully have been folded into one supercard, meaning that in a couple of months we’ll be getting to see Spike Hellis, Normal Bias, Buzz Kull, and Kontravoid all on the same night. A complete murderer’s row of modern EBM to be sure, but if you’re in NA you’ll likely have a chance to check out one if not both component parts as they’re extensive tours covering most of the continent. Hell, Spike Hellis is already on the road in support of the killer LP which finally dropped last week. Check the dates and grab tickets while listening to this week’s tracks. Are you Knormalled enough? Soft Vein, “Another Summer” Did you listen to our interview with Soft Vein on the podcast last week? If not, you should go do that right now, then come back here and listen to the exceptional “Another Summer”, yet another absolute stunner from the forthcoming All We’ve Known of Heaven. Justin Chamberlain’s songwriting, intimate style of performance and instrumentation keeps getting more undeniable with each release, and given the massive leaps he’s made in a mere three years, the overcast but beautiful skies are the limit for this melancholic LA based artist. One of our most hotly anticipated albums this year. All We've Known of Heaven by Soft Vein Patriarchy, “Bite Marks” Patriarchy are the enfants terrible of modern American darkwave, an act that provokes on stage and on record with each release. The thing is, the material backs it up, with last year’s excellent Manual For Dying showing off just how good the LA trio fronted by Actually Huizenga has gotten at bringing their gnarly stage show to their records. New EP Appendices is no different, featuring five tracks of mechanized shock rock and electro, expect to hear “Bite Marks” on your stompier dancefloors soonish. Appendices by Patriarchy Caustic, “Not Going Anywhere (Klack mix)” North American cult industrial impresario Matt Fanale follows up his last double LP Fiend with a remix album Unfiended, featuring a diverse roster of collaborators including Male Tears, Petrol Bastard, Alien Faktor, and Mark Pistel (!!!) amongst others. Of course Matt’s other project Klack dips in, bringing some of that new beat NRG to “Not Going Anywhere”, resolutely funky and full of more orch hits than a synclavier sample library. Giddy up! UNFIENDED by Caustic ner.ogris, “A View” German acts ner.ogris (or ner\ogris) have won us over via one LP and one EP of rock-solid electro-industrial which opts for considered grooves and sculpted sound design rather than shock or excess. This brooding taster from forthcoming LP Femme Fatale gets their strengths over quickly and artfully and bodes well for another course of proper home cooking from the pair. FAME FATALE by ner.ogris Knormalled, “The Servitor” The second EP from Indianapolis producer Knormalled shows a canny knack for a moody hybrid of dark electro and EBM which puts a premium on mood and slowly sliding timbral colour. Thru might best be appreciated as a full EP listen, but you can get a decent sense of the vibes from this shuddering slice. Should likely appeal if you’ve dug recent records by Kurs, or are still burning a candle for Distorted Memory. KNORMALLED THRU by Knormalled Ikon, “The Witness Tree” Some nice and easy summer goth rock from the always understated Aussie masters Ikon. Somewhat confusingly previewed then withdrawn, “The Witness Tree” is the first new material from Chris McCarter & co. in a few years and is setting up a forthcoming singles collection covering the entirety of the McCarter helmed era of the band. B-side’s got some dreamy pep, too. The Witness Tree single by IKON The post Tracks: August 10th, 2026 appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 本期乐评围绕北美秋季联合巡演展开，将Spike Hellis、Normal Bias、Buzz Kull和Kontravoid四组现代EBM艺人合并为一场演出。曲目推荐涵盖多张新作：Soft Vein的"Another Summer"延续其亲密的暗潮创作路线，编曲与器乐编排日益成熟；Patriarchy的新EP《Appendices》延续舞台化的机械冲击美学，融合shock rock与电子节奏；Caustic的remix专辑《Unfiended》汇聚Klack、Male Tears等多位合作者，将new beat律动注入工业框架；德国双人组ner.ogris的Femme Fatale预告曲展示了精细雕琢的electro-industrial质感。整体侧重于北美元素与德式工业的交叉，偏向节奏驱动型的暗潮与电子工业交融。
